text: [Page 1] CHRONIC & PERMANENT DISEASE MANAGEMENT Diabetes | Hypertension | Heart Failure | Asthma | Epilepsy | Hypothyroidism Clinical Guideline for AI Model Training Data Version 1 Sources: WHO Primary Care Guidelines | MSF Clinical Guidelines | Hesperian Health Guides | WHO Integrated Management of Adult Illness Chronic diseases require ongoing management even in conflict and low-resource settings.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:1
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Treatment goals shift to symptom control, preventing life-threatening complications, and maintaining function when specialist care and medication supplies are limited or interrupted.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:2
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: This guideline focuses on non-pharmacological and low-resource approaches.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:3:0
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DIABETES MELLITUS 1.1 Recognition Feature Type 1 (Insulin-Dependent) Type 2 (Non-Insulin-Dependent) Onset Usually sudden, younger patients Gradual, usually adults over 40 Build Often thin / normal weight Often overweight Key symptoms Excessive thirst, frequent urination, rapid weight Same symptoms but milder

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:3:1
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: may be detected only at loss, blurred vision, fatigue complication stage Emergency sign Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, altered Confusion, extreme thirst, very high blood sugar consciousness (DKA) (HHS) 1.2 Acute Complication: Hypoglycaemia (Low Blood Sugar) Most dangerous acute complication in the field.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:4
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Caused by missed meals, excess physical exertion, or over-treatment.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:5
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Stage Signs & Symptoms Low-Resource Management Mild Shaking, sweating, hunger, dizziness, palpitations If conscious: give sugar in any form 34 teaspoons of sugar dissolved in water, fruit juice, sweet tea, or honey.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:6
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Repeat after 15 minutes if no improvement.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:7
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Moderate Confusion, difficulty walking, aggressive behaviour Same as mild if can swallow.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:8
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Do NOT give food or drink if consciousness is impaired risk of choking.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:9
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Severe Unconscious, seizures, cannot swallow Place in recovery position.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:10
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Rub sugar, jam, or honey on inside of cheek and gums if semi-conscious.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:11
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: 1.3 Acute Complication: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) Type 1 (cid:127) Signs: rapid deep breathing (Kussmaul), fruity or acetone breath, vomiting, abdominal pain, progressive drowsiness.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:12
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Low-resource management: keep airway patent; position on side if drowsy; encourage oral fluids if conscious.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:13
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Urgent referral DKA is life-threatening and requires IV fluids and insulin.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:14
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Monitor breathing and level of consciousness during transport.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:15
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: 1.4 Long-Term Low-Resource Care Principles (cid:127) Dietary control: reduce sugar, white flour, white rice; increase vegetables, legumes, whole grains.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:16
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Regular physical activity: 30 minutes of walking most days if possible.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:17
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Foot care: inspect feet daily; treat any wound promptly; never walk barefoot.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:18
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: [Page 2] (cid:127) Eye and kidney complications: monitor vision and urine output; refer any visual change or leg swelling.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0:19
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_0
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Fasting during conflict: advise patients not

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:0
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Regular physical activity: 30 minutes of walking most days if possible.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:1
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Foot care: inspect feet daily; treat any wound promptly; never walk barefoot.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:2
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: [Page 2] (cid:127) Eye and kidney complications: monitor vision and urine output; refer any visual change or leg swelling.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:3
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Fasting during conflict: advise patients not to skip meals; adjust food intake rather than eliminate.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:4
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Infection risk: any infection worsens blood sugar control treat infections early.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:5
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT stop insulin abruptly in Type 1 diabetes life-threatening DKA will follow within hours.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:6
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT give anything by mouth to an unconscious diabetic patient.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:7
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT ignore foot wounds infection can progress rapidly to gangrene.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:8
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: HYPERTENSION (HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE) 2.1 Classification Category Systolic (mmHg) Diastolic (mmHg) Action Normal < 120 < 80 No action needed Elevated 120129 < 80 Lifestyle modification Stage 1 130139 8089 Lifestyle + monitor Stage 2 140 90 Treatment required Hypertensive crisis 180 120 Emergency immediate care 2.2 Hypertensive Emergency Recognition (cid:127) Severe headache, blurred vision, chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion, facial droop, or one-sided weakness.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:9
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Any blood pressure 180/120 mmHg with organ damage symptoms = hypertensive emergency.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:10
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Stroke symptoms with high blood pressure: act as stroke emergency (see Neurological Emergencies guideline).

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:11
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: 2.3 Non-Pharmacological Management (Low-Resource Setting) (cid:127) Reduce salt intake avoid adding salt to food; avoid preserved or canned foods when possible.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:12
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) DASH-style diet: increase vegetables, fruit, and legumes; reduce animal fat.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:13
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Weight reduction if overweight: even modest weight loss reduces blood pressure.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:14
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Physical activity: 30 minutes of brisk walking most days reduces systolic BP by 58 mmHg.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:15
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Reduce stress: relaxation techniques, breathing exercises, social support.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:16
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Avoid alcohol and tobacco.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:17
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Monitor blood pressure regularly if a device is available.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:18
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Continued medication supply is critical interruption causes dangerous rebound hypertension.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:19
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT abruptly stop antihypertensive medications severe rebound hypertension can cause stroke.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:20
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Hypertensive emergency with neurological signs = treat as stroke until proven otherwise.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:21
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: High blood pressure alone without symptoms does NOT require emergency treatment reduce gradually.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1:22
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_1
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: HEART FAILURE 3.1 Recognition Symptom Description Severity Indicator Breathlessness Shortness of breath on exertion; later at rest or lying flat Lying flat impossible = severe Leg oedema Swelling of ankles and legs, pitting on pressure Swelling above knee = severe Fatigue Severe tiredness with minimal effort Unable to perform daily activities Cough Persistent cough, may produce frothy or pink-tinged Pink frothy sputum = acute

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:0
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: later at rest or lying flat Lying flat impossible = severe Leg oedema Swelling of ankles and legs, pitting on pressure Swelling above knee = severe Fatigue Severe tiredness with minimal effort Unable to perform daily activities Cough Persistent cough, may produce frothy or pink-tinged Pink frothy sputum = acute pulmonary oedema sputum [Page 3] Rapid heartbeat Palpitations, irregular pulse Irregular pulse = refer urgently 3.2 Acute Pulmonary Oedema Emergency Management STEP 1 POSITION Sit the patient upright legs dangling down if possible.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:1
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Upright position reduces fluid in lungs.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:2
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 2 OXYGEN Administer high-flow oxygen if available.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:3
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Fan the patient's face if no oxygen.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:4
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 3 REDUCE EXERTION Complete rest.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:5
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: No physical effort whatsoever until stabilised.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:6
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 4 RESTRICT FLUIDS Do not give oral fluids beyond small sips.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:7
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: No IV fluids unless specifically required.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:8
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 5 REFER URGENTLY Acute pulmonary oedema is life-threatening.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:9
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Arrange emergency evacuation.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:10
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: 3.3 Ongoing Low-Resource Management (cid:127) Salt restriction: reduce sodium intake most important non-pharmacological measure.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:11
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Fluid restriction: in severe heart failure, limit fluid intake to 11.5 litres per day.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:12
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Elevate legs: when resting, elevate legs above heart level to reduce oedema.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:13
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Daily weight monitoring: sudden weight gain of > 1 kg overnight indicates fluid retention restrict fluids and rest.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:14
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Avoid exertion in heat: hot weather increases cardiovascular strain.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:15
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Sleeping position: sleep with upper body elevated on folded clothing or blankets.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:16
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Avoid lying flat: use inclined sleeping position if orthopnoea (breathlessness lying flat) is present.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:17
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT lay a patient with acute breathlessness flat worsens pulmonary oedema immediately.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:18
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT give excess IV fluids to a patient with known heart failure.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:19:0
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: EPILEPSY SEIZURE MANAGEMENT 4.1 Types of Seizures Type Appearance Duration Generalised tonic-clonic (grand Stiffening of whole body followed by jerking of arms and legs

text: Usually 13 minutes mal) loss of consciousness

source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: urinary incontinence Absence seizure (petit mal) Sudden brief staring, unresponsive, eyelid fluttering

chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: no fall 530 seconds Focal (partial) seizure Jerking limited to one limb or side

source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: may or may not Seconds to minutes lose consciousness Status epilepticus Continuous seizure lasting > 5 minutes OR two seizures without Medical emergency recovery between 4.2 First Aid During a Seizure STEP 1 PROTECT FROM INJURY Clear the area of hard or sharp objects.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:20
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Place something soft under the head folded clothing.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2:21
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_2
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Do NOT restrain the person.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:0
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: lasting > 5 minutes OR two seizures without Medical emergency recovery between 4.2 First Aid During a Seizure STEP 1 PROTECT FROM INJURY Clear the area of hard or sharp objects.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:1
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Place something soft under the head folded clothing.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:2
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Do NOT restrain the person.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:3
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: [Page 4] STEP 2 TIME THE SEIZURE Note exact time seizure began.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:4
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: If > 5 minutes, this is status epilepticus life-threatening emergency.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:5
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 3 AIRWAY Do NOT put anything in the mouth.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:6
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Do NOT try to hold the tongue.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:7
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Tongue biting cannot be prevented by finger insertion and this causes injury to helper.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:8
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 4 RECOVERY POSITION When jerking stops, place patient on their side (recovery position) to prevent aspiration of saliva or vomit.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:9
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: STEP 5 POST-ICTAL PHASE Patient may be confused, sleepy, or agitated for minutes to hours after seizure.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:10
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: 4.3 Status Epilepticus (Seizure > 5 Minutes) Emergency (cid:127) Seizure lasting > 5 minutes or repeated seizures without recovery = status epilepticus.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:11
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Maintain airway; recovery position; high-flow oxygen if available.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:12
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Prevent injury; keep environment safe.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:13
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer immediately requires emergency medical intervention.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:14
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) If diazepam rectal solution is available per protocol: use per MSF guidelines.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:15
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: No pharmacological guidance included here.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:16
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT restrain seizure movements causes fractures and dislocations.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:17
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT place objects or fingers in the mouth during a seizure.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:18
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: DO NOT give food or water until patient is fully conscious.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:19
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: Seizure > 5 minutes = life-threatening emergency seek help immediately.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:20
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: HYPOTHYROIDISM 5.1 Recognition (cid:127) Fatigue, weakness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, hair loss, weight gain, slow heartbeat.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:21
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) In severe or untreated cases: puffy face, slowed thinking, depression, hoarse voice.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:22
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) Myxoedema coma (extreme hypothyroidism): confusion, hypothermia, very slow heartbeat, decreased consciousness.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:23
chunk_id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3
source: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline
text: (cid:127) In conflict settings: iodine deficiency is a major cause goitre (enlarged thyroid) may be visible.

id: 01_chronic_diseases_guideline_chunk_3:24

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: [Page 1] BREATHING & CHEST PROBLEMS Respiratory Distress | Asthma | Pneumonia | Pneumothorax | Chest Wounds Clinical Guideline for AI Model Training Data Version 1 Sources: WHO IMAI | MSF Clinical Guidelines | Hesperian Health Guides | ICRC War Surgery | WHO ARI Guidelines Respiratory emergencies are among the most rapidly fatal conditions in any setting.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:1
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Correct patient positioning, airway management, and early recognition of life-threatening chest injury are critical skills in conflict and low-resource environments where mechanical ventilation is unavailable.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:2
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: RECOGNISING RESPIRATORY DISTRESS UNIVERSAL SIGNS Sign Description Severity Indicator Respiratory rate Normal adult: 1220 breaths/min.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:3:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: < 10 or > 30 = danger Accessory muscle use Neck muscles, shoulder muscles, or abdominal muscles Sign of significant distress straining with each breath Nasal flaring Nostrils widening with each breath especially significant in Moderatesevere distress children Chest wall retractions Skin sucking in between ribs, at neck, or below ribcage Moderatesevere distress Cyanosis Blue discolouration of lips, tongue, fingernails Severe hypoxia emergency Unable to speak Cannot complete a full sentence due to breathlessness Severe near-emergency Altered consciousness Confusion, agitation, drowsiness in a patient with breathing Pre-arrest emergency difficulty Silent chest No breath sounds on auscultation or no visible chest Life-threatening emergency movement 2.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:4
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: AIRWAY MANAGEMENT LOW-RESOURCE STEP 1 OPEN THE AIRWAY Tilt head back and lift chin (head-tilt chin-lift).

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:5
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: In trauma: jaw thrust without head tilt to protect spine.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:6
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 2 CLEAR THE AIRWAY Remove visible foreign material with finger sweep.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:7
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Roll patient onto side to drain blood or vomit.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:8
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 3 RECOVERY POSITION Unconscious patient breathing: roll onto side.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:9
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: This prevents airway obstruction from tongue and aspiration of vomit.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:10
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 4 POSITIONING FOR BREATHLESSNESS Conscious patient who is breathless: sit upright, leaning slightly forward (tripod position).

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:11
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 5 OXYGEN Administer high-flow oxygen if available.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:12
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Fan the face if no oxygen mild improvement in perceived breathlessness.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:13
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: ASTHMA 3.1 Recognition Feature MildModerate Attack Severe / Life-Threatening Attack Speech Can speak in sentences Single words only or cannot speak Breathing rate Increased but < 25/min > 25/min Wheeze Present expiratory wheeze Silent chest no wheeze = very severe Position Can lie down / walk Unable to lie down; hunched forward Consciousness Alert Confused, drowsy, or agitated Lips/nails Normal colour Blue (cyanosis) emergency 3.2 Management (cid:127) Sit the patient upright forward-leaning position reduces work of breathing.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0:14
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_0
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Remove from trigger: smoke, dust, animals, cold

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: no wheeze = very severe Position Can lie down / walk Unable to lie down; hunched forward Consciousness Alert Confused, drowsy, or agitated Lips/nails Normal colour Blue (cyanosis) emergency 3.2 Management (cid:127) Sit the patient upright forward-leaning position reduces work of breathing.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:1
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Remove from trigger: smoke, dust, animals, cold air, chemical fumes.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:2
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Calm the patient anxiety worsens bronchospasm.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:3
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Salbutamol inhaler (if available): 48 puffs via spacer or improvised spacer (plastic bottle).

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:4
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: See MSF protocols for dosing.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:5
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Improvised spacer: cut the bottom off a 500 mL plastic bottle; insert inhaler in mouthpiece end; breathe through bottle neck.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:6
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Life-threatening attack (silent chest, cyanosis, confusion): emergency referral requires IV bronchodilators.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:7
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Triggers to avoid long-term: smoke, cold air, dust, strong perfumes, exercise in cold air, respiratory infections.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:8
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: PNEUMONIA 4.1 Recognition Sign/Symptom Description Significance Cough Productive cough with yellow, green, or rust-coloured sputum Common presentation Fever Temperature > 38C Present in most bacterial pneumonia Rapid breathing Adult: > 20/min.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:9:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Child: > 50/min (< 2 months)

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:9:1
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: > 40/min (212 Most reliable clinical sign months)

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:9:2
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: > 30/min (15 years) Chest pain Sharp pain worse on breathing or coughing (pleuritic) Indicates pleural involvement Reduced air entry Breath sounds reduced or absent on one side dullness on Consolidation or effusion percussion Confusion (elderly) New onset confusion in elderly patient with fever and cough High mortality risk = pneumonia until proven otherwise 4.2 Severity Assessment CURB-65 (Simplified) (cid:127) C Confusion: new onset confusion (cid:127) U Urea > 7 mmol/L (lab not always available) (cid:127) R Respiratory rate 30/min (cid:127) B BP systolic < 90 or diastolic 60 mmHg (cid:127) 65 Age 65 years (cid:127) Score 01: likely manageable with outpatient antibiotics.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:10
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Score 2: consider inpatient care.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:11
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Score 3: severe urgent care needed.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:12
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: 4.3 Low-Resource Supportive Management [Page 3] (cid:127) Position upright or semi-recumbent improves ventilation and reduces aspiration risk.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:13
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Hydration: encourage oral fluids prevents dehydration and helps liquefy secretions.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:14
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Breathing exercises: deep breathing and coughing exercises every 2 hours helps clear secretions.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:15
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Fever management: cooling with damp cloths; oral paracetamol if available.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:16
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Antibiotics are required prescribe per MSF/WHO guidelines for pneumonia.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:17
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Supportive care alone is insufficient for bacterial pneumonia.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:18
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Monitor breathing rate every 46 hours worsening rate indicates treatment failure.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:19
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer any patient who cannot take oral fluids, has cyanosis, or CURB-65 2.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1:20
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_1
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCY 5.1 Recognition A tension pneumothorax occurs when air accumulates

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Supportive care alone is insufficient for bacterial pneumonia.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:1
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Monitor breathing rate every 46 hours worsening rate indicates treatment failure.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:2
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer any patient who cannot take oral fluids, has cyanosis, or CURB-65 2.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:3
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCY 5.1 Recognition A tension pneumothorax occurs when air accumulates under pressure in the pleural space, collapsing the lung and compressing the heart and great vessels.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:4
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Death follows within minutes if untreated.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:5:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Sign Description Absent breath sounds No breath sounds on one side of the chest Tracheal deviation Trachea deviated AWAY from the affected side (late sign may not be present) Hypotension + distended neck veins Shock with raised jugular venous pressure Increasing respiratory distress Rapidly worsening breathlessness, cyanosis, altered consciousness Mechanism Penetrating chest wound, blunt trauma, rib fractures, blast injury 5.2 Emergency Management Needle Decompression Needle decompression is life-saving and can be performed in the field with basic equipment when tension pneumothorax is suspected clinically.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:6
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 1 CONFIRM CLINICALLY Do NOT wait for imaging.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:7
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Clinical signs of tension pneumothorax = act immediately.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:8
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 2 POSITION Patient semi-recumbent or sitting if possible.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:9
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 3 NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION Insert large-bore needle (1416 G if available) into 2nd intercostal space, mid-clavicular line, superior border of the rib (avoid neurovascular bundle below each rib).

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:10
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Rush of air = confirms diagnosis.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:11
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 4 SEAL AND REFER Apply occlusive dressing.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:12
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Arrange immediate surgical referral for definitive chest drain.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:13
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: OPEN CHEST WOUNDS (SUCKING CHEST WOUND) An open chest wound allows air to enter the pleural space with each breath, collapsing the lung on that side.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:14
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: It can rapidly progress to tension pneumothorax.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:15
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 1 SEAL THREE SIDES Apply an occlusive dressing (plastic wrap, foil, clean plastic bag) and tape THREE sides only, leaving one side open.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:16
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: This creates a one-way valve air exits on expiration but cannot enter on inspiration.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:17
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: [Page 4] STEP 2 MONITOR BREATHING Watch for signs of tension pneumothorax developing (worsening distress, tracheal deviation).

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:18
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: If these develop, briefly lift the unsealed edge to release pressure.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:19
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 3 POSITION Sit patient upright.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:20
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: Keep affected side down if possible.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:21
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: STEP 4 REFER URGENTLY All open chest wounds require surgical management.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:22
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: RIB FRACTURES & FLAIL CHEST 7.1 Single / Multiple Rib Fractures (cid:127) Pain localised to fracture site, worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:23
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Patient may splint the chest (hold side and breathe shallowly) this increases pneumonia risk.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2:24
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_2
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Management: analgesia to allow deep

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:0
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: chest wounds require surgical management.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:1
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: RIB FRACTURES & FLAIL CHEST 7.1 Single / Multiple Rib Fractures (cid:127) Pain localised to fracture site, worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:2
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Patient may splint the chest (hold side and breathe shallowly) this increases pneumonia risk.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:3
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Management: analgesia to allow deep breathing; encourage deep breaths and coughing every hour.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:4
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Circumferential chest binding is CONTRAINDICATED restricts breathing and worsens outcome.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:5
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer if > 3 ribs fractured, elderly patient, or any respiratory compromise.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:6
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: 7.2 Flail Chest Flail chest occurs when multiple adjacent ribs are broken in two places, creating a free-floating segment.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:7
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: This segment moves paradoxically (inward on inspiration, outward on expiration), severely impairing ventilation.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:8
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Recognition: paradoxical chest wall movement visible on examination.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:9
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Apply gentle manual stabilisation over the flail segment if resources allow.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:10
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) Position: injured side down if possible splints the flail segment naturally.

id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3:11
chunk_id: 03_breathing_chest_guideline_chunk_3
source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: (cid:127) High-flow oxygen; analgesia; urgent referral requires positive pressure ventilation in severe cases.

source: 03_breathing_chest_guideline
text: RED FLAGS CRITERIA FOR URGENT REFERRAL Red Flag Criterion Clinical Significance / Action Silent chest / no breath sounds Severe asthma or tension pneumothorax life-threatening emergency Cyanosis Severe hypoxia oxygen immediately

text: SOFT TISSUE INJURIES SPRAINS & STRAINS 3.1 RICE Protocol STEP R REST Stop using the injured part immediately.

text: STEP I ICE / COLD Apply cold compress (ice wrapped in cloth, or cold wet cloth if no ice) for 20 minutes every 2 hours for first 48 hours.

chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_1

text: DISLOCATIONS A dislocation is the complete displacement of a joint.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:2
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: The most common are shoulder, finger, patella, and hip.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:3
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: Dislocations should be reduced as soon as possible muscle spasm worsens with time, making reduction harder.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:4
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: 4.1 General Principles (cid:127) Check and document neurovascular status BEFORE any reduction attempt.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:5
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) Adequate analgesia and muscle relaxation are important for successful reduction.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:6
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) Do NOT attempt reduction if fracture cannot be excluded risk of worsening the injury.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:7
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) After reduction: immobilise; reassess neurovascular status; refer for imaging if available.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:8
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: 4.2 Shoulder Dislocation (Anterior most common) (cid:127) Recognition: arm held away from body; loss of shoulder contour; very painful; hollow below acromion.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:9
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) Stimson technique (low-resource): patient lies face down; dangle affected arm with 510 kg weight (bag of water).

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:10
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: Gravity slowly reduces dislocation over 2030 minutes.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:11
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) External rotation method: patient supine; slowly externally rotate arm to 90 degrees, then raise.

id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2:12
chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2
source: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline
text: (cid:127) After reduction: immobilise in sling for 3 weeks; refer for reassessment.

chunk_id: 04_gi_musculoskeletal_guideline_chunk_2

source: 05_poisoning_guideline

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:4
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: GENERAL FIRST AID FOR INGESTED POISONS STEP 1 IDENTIFY THE SUBSTANCE If possible, identify what was taken, how much, and when.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:5
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Bring container or sample.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:6
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 2 DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING UNLESS SPECIFICALLY DIRECTED CONTRAINDICATED for: corrosives (acids/alkalis), petroleum products, sharp objects, or if unconscious.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:7
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Vomiting worsens corrosive burns and causes aspiration.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:8
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 3 IF CONSCIOUS AND SUBSTANCE IS NON-CORROSIVE Give 12 glasses of water or milk to dilute the substance.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:9
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Do NOT give more excess fluid causes vomiting.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:10
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 4 ACTIVATED CHARCOAL (IF AVAILABLE) Most effective within 1 hour of ingestion.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:11
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Give 1 g/kg body weight mixed in water.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:12
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: CONTRAINDICATED if corrosive ingested or unconscious.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:13
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 5 AIRWAY AND POSITION If unconscious: recovery position.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:14
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: If vomiting: roll to side.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:15
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: [Page 2] STEP 6 REFER URGENTLY All significant poisoning requires medical assessment.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:16
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Bring substance or container.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:17
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER induce vomiting for corrosive ingestion (acids, alkalis, bleach, drain cleaner) causes second burn.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:18
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER induce vomiting for petroleum products (petrol, kerosene) causes aspiration pneumonia.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0:19
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_0
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER give anything by mouth to

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:0
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: [Page 2] STEP 6 REFER URGENTLY All significant poisoning requires medical assessment.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:1
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Bring substance or container.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:2
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER induce vomiting for corrosive ingestion (acids, alkalis, bleach, drain cleaner) causes second burn.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:3
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER induce vomiting for petroleum products (petrol, kerosene) causes aspiration pneumonia.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:4
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: NEVER give anything by mouth to an unconscious patient.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:5
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: CARBON MONOXIDE POISONING 3.1 Recognition Carbon monoxide (CO) is colourless and odourless.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:6
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: It binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen, causing cellular asphyxia.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:7
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Multiple people affected in an enclosed space is a strong diagnostic clue.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:8
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Severity Symptoms Mild Headache, nausea, dizziness, weakness often mistaken for influenza Moderate Throbbing headache, confusion, chest pain, breathlessness on exertion Severe Confusion, loss of consciousness, seizures, cardiac arrhythmia, death NOTE: Pulse oximetry CANNOT detect CO poisoning reads falsely normal.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:9
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Cyanosis is often ABSENT despite severe CO poisoning.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:10
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: 3.2 Management STEP 1 REMOVE FROM EXPOSURE Immediately move patient to fresh air.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:11
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Do NOT enter contaminated space without respiratory protection.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:12
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 2 HIGH-FLOW OXYGEN Administer 100% oxygen by non-rebreather mask.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:13
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: This is the primary treatment accelerates CO elimination fourfold.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:14
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 3 AIRWAY AND RECOVERY POSITION Unconscious: recovery position; monitor airway.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:15
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Rescue breathing if respiratory arrest.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:16
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 4 REFER ALL CASES All CO poisoning requires medical assessment.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:17
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Delayed neurological effects can occur up to days later.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:18
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: ORGANOPHOSPHATE POISONING (PESTICIDES & NERVE AGENTS) Organophosphates are found in agricultural pesticides and military nerve agents (sarin, VX, etc).

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:19
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: They inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine at nerve synapses.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:20
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: 4.1 Recognition SLUDGE + Nicotinic Effects System Symptoms Muscarinic (SLUDGE) Salivation, Lacrimation (tearing), Urination, Defecation, GI cramps, Emesis Eyes Miosis (small pinpoint pupils) characteristic and early sign Lungs Bronchospasm, excessive secretions, wheezing, respiratory failure Heart Bradycardia (slow heart rate) Nicotinic (muscle) Muscle twitching (fasciculations), weakness, paralysis CNS Anxiety, seizures, loss of consciousness [Page 3] 4.2 Management STEP 1 RESCUER SAFETY FIRST Do NOT touch the patient without gloves and face protection.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:21
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Organophosphates absorb through skin.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:22
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 2 REMOVE FROM EXPOSURE Remove all contaminated clothing (outdoors).

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:23
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Flush skin and eyes with large amounts of water for 15 minutes.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:24
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 3 AIRWAY AND BREATHING Most critical bronchospasm and secretions cause respiratory failure.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:25
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Suction secretions if equipment available.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:26
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Rescue breathing if needed.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:27
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 4 ATROPINE (IF AVAILABLE) Atropine is the antidote.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:28
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Administer per MSF / ICRC nerve agent protocol.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:29
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: In low-resource settings without atropine: supportive airway management.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1:30
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_1
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 5 SEIZURE MANAGEMENT Position safely; prevent injury; do not restrain.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:0
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Suction secretions if equipment available.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:1
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Rescue breathing if needed.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:2
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 4 ATROPINE (IF AVAILABLE) Atropine is the antidote.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:3
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Administer per MSF / ICRC nerve agent protocol.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:4
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: In low-resource settings without atropine: supportive airway management.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:5
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 5 SEIZURE MANAGEMENT Position safely; prevent injury; do not restrain.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:6
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Recovery position after seizure.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:7
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 6 URGENT REFERRAL All organophosphate poisoning requires urgent medical care.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:8
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: SNAKEBITE 5.1 Recognition of Envenomation Type of Snake Key Features Dominant Effect Viper (most common globally) Severe local pain and swelling starting within minutes; Local tissue destruction + blistering; tissue destruction coagulopathy (bleeding) Cobra / elapid Less local swelling; neurological symptoms dominant Paralysis, respiratory failure Sea snake Muscle pain; dark urine (myoglobinuria); weakness Muscle breakdown 5.2 First Aid Management STEP 1 IMMOBILISE THE PATIENT Keep the bitten limb still and at heart level.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:9
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Immobilise as you would a fracture.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:10
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Movement accelerates venom absorption.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:11
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 2 CALM AND REASSURE Most snakebites are from non-venomous species.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:12
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Panic increases heart rate and venom spread.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:13
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 3 REMOVE CONSTRICTING ITEMS Remove rings, watches, bracelets from the bitten limb before swelling.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:14
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: STEP 4 MARK AND MONITOR SWELLING Mark the edge of swelling with a pen and note the time.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:15
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Rapidly advancing swelling = envenomation.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:16
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: [Page 4] STEP 5 REFER URGENTLY Transport to nearest facility with antivenom.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:17
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Keep patient still during transport.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:18
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: DO NOT cut and suck the wound causes infection and is ineffective.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:19
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: DO NOT apply tourniquet causes limb ischaemia and worsens outcome.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:20
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: DO NOT apply electric shock no evidence and causes burns.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:21
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: DO NOT apply ice worsens tissue damage.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:22
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: Antivenom is the only effective treatment for significant envenomation.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:23
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: CORROSIVE INGESTION (ACIDS & ALKALIS) (cid:127) Burns to lips, mouth, tongue white or red discolouration.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:24
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) Drooling, difficulty swallowing, severe throat pain, hoarse voice.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:25
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) Chest or abdominal pain.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:26
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) DO NOT induce vomiting causes second-degree burn on the way back up.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:27
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) Give small sips of water or milk ONLY to dilute; do not give large volumes.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:28
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) Secure airway swelling can obstruct airway rapidly.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:29
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer urgently requires endoscopy to assess oesophageal injury.

id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2:30
chunk_id: 05_poisoning_guideline_chunk_2
source: 05_poisoning_guideline
text: RED FLAGS CRITERIA FOR URGENT REFERRAL Red Flag Criterion Clinical Significance / Action Respiratory failure (any cause) Slowing breathing, cyanosis, or unconsciousness from any poison Organophosphate poisoning Any significant exposure rapid deterioration and respiratory failure CO poisoning Any loss of consciousness delayed neurological effects common Corrosive ingestion Airway oedema risk refer even if currently speaking normally

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:0
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: [Page 1] NEUROLOGICAL EMERGENCIES Stroke | Seizure | Meningitis | Head Injury | Loss of Consciousness Clinical Guideline for AI Model Training Data Version 1 Sources: WHO Stroke Guidelines | MSF Clinical Guidelines | WHO mhGAP | Hesperian Health Guides | ICRC War Surgery Neurological emergencies require rapid recognition and early action.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:1
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: In conflict settings where CT imaging and specialist care are unavailable, clinical recognition and appropriate first aid can be the difference between survival with good function and death or permanent disability.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:2:0
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: STROKE (CEREBROVASCULAR ACCIDENT CVA) 1.1 FAST Recognition Tool Letter Test Positive Finding F Face Ask person to smile One side of face droops facial asymmetry A Arms Ask person to raise both arms with eyes One arm drifts downward or cannot be raised closed S Speech Ask person to repeat a simple sentence Slurred, wrong words, or unable to speak T Time If ANY of the above: Time is CRITICAL Note exact time symptoms began critical for treatment window 1.2 Ischaemic vs Haemorrhagic Stroke Field Differentiation Clinical differentiation between ischaemic (clot) and haemorrhagic (bleed) stroke is difficult without imaging.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:3
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Treat as stroke and refer urgently.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:4
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Feature Ischaemic Stroke (more common) Haemorrhagic Stroke Onset Often on waking or gradual Sudden during activity Headache Absent or mild Severe 'thunderclap' headache Vomiting Less common More common Consciousness Often preserved early May be impaired early Progression May stabilise or improve Often deteriorates 1.3 Management STEP 1 NOTE EXACT TIME Record time of symptom onset critical for determining eligibility for thrombolysis if available.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:5
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: STEP 2 POSITION Conscious patient: lie flat with head slightly elevated (2030 degrees).

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:6
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Do NOT raise head above 30 degrees in ischaemic stroke reduces cerebral perfusion.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:7
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: STEP 3 AIRWAY Unconscious: recovery position; ensure airway is clear of secretions.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:8
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: [Page 2] STEP 4 DO NOT GIVE FOOD OR WATER Swallowing impairment is common after stroke high aspiration risk.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:9
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Test swallow before any oral intake.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:10
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: STEP 5 DO NOT LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE AGGRESSIVELY Elevated BP after stroke is a compensatory response.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:11
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Do NOT treat high BP acutely in the field unless > 220/120.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:12
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: STEP 6 URGENT REFERRAL Stroke is a time-critical emergency.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:13
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: Stroke is not treatable in the field.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:14
chunk_id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0
source: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline
text: DO NOT give aspirin until haemorrhagic stroke is excluded aspirin worsens a bleed.

id: 06_neurological_emergencies_guideline_chunk_0:15

text: [Page 1] MENTAL HEALTH & SHOCK STATES Hypovolaemic Shock | Acute Stress | PTSD | Psychosis | Suicide Risk | Grief Clinical Guideline for AI Model Training Data Version 1 Sources: WHO mhGAP | MSF Mental Health Guidelines | IASC MHPSS | Sphere Handbook | Hesperian Health Guides In conflict and disaster settings, both physiological shock and psychological trauma are common and often occur together.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_0:1
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_0
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: This guideline covers recognition and low-resource management of hypovolaemic shock, and the most common acute and chronic mental health presentations in affected populations.

text: HYPOVOLAEMIC SHOCK RECOGNITION & MANAGEMENT Hypovolaemic shock results from loss of blood or fluid volume.

source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Most people recover naturally within days.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:10
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Feature Description Emotional symptoms Anxiety, fear, panic, anger, tearfulness, emotional numbness, feeling detached from surroundings Physical symptoms Palpitations, trembling, sweating, nausea, headache, dizziness Cognitive symptoms Difficulty concentrating, confusion, disorientation, intrusive memories Behavioural symptoms Withdrawal, hyperactivity, risk-taking, searching behaviour (in bereavement) Duration Hours to days if > 4 weeks, consider PTSD 2.1 Psychological First Aid (PFA) Low-Resource Approach STEP L LOOK Observe the person.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:11
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Are they in acute distress?

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:12
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Do they need immediate practical help?

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:13
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: STEP L LISTEN Approach calmly.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:14
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Ask open questions: 'How are you feeling?' Do not force the person to talk.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:15
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: STEP L LINK Help them access practical support: food, water, shelter, family contact, medical care.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:16
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Link to community and family.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:17
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Do NOT debrief do not ask the person to retell traumatic events in detail.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:18
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Do NOT give false reassurance ('everything will be okay').

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:19
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Do validate feelings: 'It is completely normal to feel this way after what you have been through.' (cid:127) Ensure basic needs first: safety, water, food, warmth, contact with family.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:20
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Most people recover without formal mental health treatment.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:21
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) PTSD may develop weeks or months after traumatic events.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:22
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: It is distinct from normal grief or sadness.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1:23
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_1
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Symptom Cluster Common Presentations Re-experiencing Flashbacks (involuntary vivid memories of trauma); nightmares; emotional distress triggered by reminders [Page 3] Avoidance Avoiding thoughts, feelings, people, or places associated with trauma Hyperarousal Constant alertness (hypervigilance), easily startled, difficulty sleeping, irritability, anger outbursts Negative cognition Persistent guilt, shame, self-blame; negative

text: emotional distress triggered by reminders [Page 3] Avoidance Avoiding thoughts, feelings, people, or places associated with trauma Hyperarousal Constant alertness (hypervigilance), easily startled, difficulty sleeping, irritability, anger outbursts Negative cognition Persistent guilt, shame, self-blame

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:0:2

text: emotional numbness Diagnosis requires Symptoms > 1 month

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:0:4
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: significant impairment in daily functioning 3.1 Low-Resource Support (cid:127) Psychoeducation: explain that PTSD is a normal response to abnormal events not a sign of weakness.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:1
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Re-establish routine: regular daily activities, meals, sleep schedule.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:2
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Social support: encourage connection with family, community, and cultural or religious practices.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:3
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Physical activity: regular walking or exercise significantly reduces PTSD symptoms.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:4
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Relaxation techniques: slow deep breathing (4 counts in, hold 4, out 4); grounding techniques (name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear).

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:5
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Refer for psychological therapy (CBT, EMDR) if available these are first-line treatments.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:6
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) mhGAP guidelines: frontline workers can deliver brief structured interventions without specialist training.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:7
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: ACUTE PSYCHOSIS Psychosis involves loss of contact with reality.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:8
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: It may be triggered by extreme stress, sleep deprivation, substance use, or underlying psychiatric illness.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:9
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: In conflict settings it may be mistaken for possession or spiritual illness.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:10
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Feature Description Hallucinations Hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot perceive Delusions Fixed false beliefs may believe they are being followed, have special powers, or that others are trying to harm them Disorganised speech Incoherent, jumping topics; words not forming meaningful sentences Disorganised behaviour Unpredictable or bizarre behaviour; difficulty with self-care Negative symptoms Flat affect, withdrawal, lack of motivation, reduced speech 4.1 Management (cid:127) Ensure safety of the person and others.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:11
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Calm, quiet environment reduce stimulation.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:12
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Speak slowly and clearly in short sentences; do not argue with delusions.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:13
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Maintain a non-threatening physical distance.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:14
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Do not leave acutely psychotic person alone.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:15
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Antipsychotic medication is required for treatment refer to mental health services.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:16
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: (cid:127) Acute psychosis may have medical causes: head injury, high fever, meningitis, substance use screen for these.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:17
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT & RESPONSE Suicide risk is elevated in conflict settings, particularly among those who have lost family, been displaced, or experienced sexual violence.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:18
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: Asking about suicide does NOT increase the risk.

id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2:19
chunk_id: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline_chunk_2
source: 07_mental_health_shock_guideline
text: 5.1 Risk Assessment Risk Level Indicators Response Passive ideation Wishes to be dead; feels life is not worth living;
