id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Explain this clearly to the person.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Moving one eye moves both.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Neck Injuries from Shrapnel Source: TCCC Guidelines; ATLS 10th Edition Neck Trauma.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The neck contains the largest blood vessels in the body (carotid arteries and jugular veins), the airway (trachea), and the spinal cord.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: A shrapnel wound to the neck can kill in under 2 minutes from bleeding alone.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS OF DANGEROUS NECK INJURY Active bleeding from the neck even moderate bleeding here is life-threatening Expanding swelling or bruising in the neck (blood pooling under skin) Hoarse voice, difficulty speaking, or stridor (high-pitched breathing sound) Difficulty swallowing or speaking after a neck wound Bubbling or hissing from a neck wound (trachea/airway injury) IMMEDIATE ACTIONS 90.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DIRECT PRESSURE ONLY: Press clean cloth firmly over the bleeding area.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_11
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Use firm sustained pressure.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: under skin) Hoarse voice, difficulty speaking, or stridor (high-pitched breathing sound) Difficulty swallowing or speaking after a neck wound Bubbling or hissing from a neck wound (trachea/airway injury) IMMEDIATE ACTIONS 90.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DIRECT PRESSURE ONLY: Press clean cloth firmly over the bleeding area.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Use firm sustained pressure.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: NEVER USE A TOURNIQUET ON THE NECK: A tourniquet around the neck stops blood flow to the brain and kills instantly.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT PACK AGGRESSIVELY: Deep packing of neck wounds risks compressing the airway or causing further vessel damage.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Apply surface pressure only.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: MONITOR THE AIRWAY: Watch continuously for signs of airway difficulty noisy breathing, blue lips, inability to speak.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If breathing worsens, open the airway (head tilt/chin lift, see Section 5B) and be ready to give rescue breaths.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: KEEP HEAD STILL: Avoid unnecessary movement of the neck.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If spinal injury is possible (blast threw the person), keep the head and neck aligned.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY: Neck injuries are among the highest-priority evacuations.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: [Page 16] A neck wound that appears small can still be cutting a major vessel internally.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Do not be reassured by a small external wound.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Treat all neck wounds as life- threatening.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Abdominal Shrapnel Injury Source: ICRC War Surgery; NATO Emergency War Surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Shrapnel penetrating the abdomen causes the same internal injuries as a gunshot wound to the abdomen.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: There is no field treatment for internal abdominal bleeding only stabilization and evacuation.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS Entry wound on the abdomen, side, or lower back Belly becomes progressively hard, rigid, and painful Signs of shock: pale, sweating, rapid weak pulse, confusion Visible bowel or tissue protruding from wound FIELD CARE 96.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT pack the abdominal wound deeply with cloth this worsens internal injury.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT push any protruding tissue back inside.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COVER the wound loosely with the cleanest damp material available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If an object is embedded: stabilize it with padding on all sides do not remove.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: NOTHING BY MOUTH: No water, no food surgery will be needed.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: LAY FLAT: Allow knees to bend if more comfortable.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TREAT FOR SHOCK: Keep warm, elevate legs gently.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:25
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE URGENTLY: Internal abdominal injuries are universally fatal without surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:26
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Multiple Small Wounds Triage Priority Source: TCCC Tactical Field Care Guidelines; NATO Mass Casualty Management.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12:27
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_12
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: In blast events, a single person may have 20 or more separate fragment wounds.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Keep warm, elevate legs gently.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE URGENTLY: Internal abdominal injuries are universally fatal without surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Multiple Small Wounds Triage Priority Source: TCCC Tactical Field Care Guidelines; NATO Mass Casualty Management.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: In blast events, a single person may have 20 or more separate fragment wounds.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The natural instinct is to address the most visible wound.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The most visible wound is often not the most dangerous one.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: [Page 17] THE CORRECT APPROACH 104.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EXPOSE THE WHOLE BODY: Before treating any single wound, quickly cut or remove clothing to view the entire body surface.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This takes 3060 seconds and saves lives.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: FIND THE BIGGEST BLEED FIRST: Look for the wound with the fastest active bleeding.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: A wound soaking cloth in seconds outranks one that is oozing slowly.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: USE THE ZONE TABLE (Section 2A): Identify which zone the worst wound is in and prioritize accordingly.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TREAT LIFE THREATS IN ORDER: Massive bleeding airway breathing all other wounds.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: MARK TREATED WOUNDS: Use pen, chalk, or mud to mark wounds that have been dressed so nothing is missed.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Small wounds in critical zones (neck, chest, abdomen) are more dangerous than large wounds on the arms and legs.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Infection Risk from Shrapnel Wounds Source: ICRC War Surgery; WHO Wound Management Guidelines.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Shrapnel carries dirt, clothing fibers, and bacteria deep into tissue.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: All shrapnel wounds are considered contaminated.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Infection typically develops 2472 hours after injury and can become life-threatening within days without antibiotics.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS OF WOUND INFECTION (appearing 2472 hours later) Increasing redness spreading from the wound edges Increasing pain and swelling around the wound Warmth around the wound Pus or cloudy discharge from the wound Red streaks extending from the wound toward the body (sign of spreading infection emergency) Fever, chills, increasing weakness FIELD PREVENTION AND CARE 109.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RINSE ALL WOUNDS WITH CLEAN WATER immediately after injury.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Use as much as available irrigation reduces infection risk more than any other field measure.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COVER WITH CLEAN DRY MATERIAL: All wounds should be covered to keep them clean.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT CLOSE DIRTY WOUNDS: Do not tie, tape, or suture shrapnel wounds closed in the field.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Trapping contamination inside causes gangrene.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:25
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CHANGE DRESSINGS DAILY if possible, using the cleanest available material each time.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:26
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: IF INFECTION DEVELOPS: Evacuate.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13:27
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_13
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Field treatment cannot adequately treat deep wound infection.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DIRTY WOUNDS: Do not tie, tape, or suture shrapnel wounds closed in the field.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Trapping contamination inside causes gangrene.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CHANGE DRESSINGS DAILY if possible, using the cleanest available material each time.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: IF INFECTION DEVELOPS: Evacuate.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Field treatment cannot adequately treat deep wound infection.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RED STREAKS FROM A WOUND: This is a medical emergency.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Septicemia (blood poisoning) can develop within hours.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Do not close shrapnel wounds.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Closed contaminated wounds can cause fatal gas gangrene.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Fractures Caused by Shrapnel Impact Source: PHTLS 9th Edition; NATO Emergency War Surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: High-velocity fragments carry enough energy to shatter bone even when they do not penetrate deeply.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: An open fracture (bone visible or wound near broken bone) is both an orthopedic and infection emergency.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS OF FRACTURE Deformity limb looks bent or out of position Inability or refusal to move the limb Severe local pain and swelling Grinding or grating sensation Bone visible through the wound (open fracture highest infection risk) FIELD CARE 115.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT STRAIGHTEN THE LIMB: Immobilize it in the position you find it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Forced straightening causes additional vessel and nerve damage.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SPLINT IN PLACE: Use any rigid material (stick, board, rolled clothing) alongside the limb and tie above and below the fracture not over it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The splint should extend beyond the joints above and below the fracture.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CHECK CIRCULATION: After splinting, check that fingers or toes below the fracture are still warm and can be felt.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If they are cold, pale, or numb, the splint may be too tight loosen slightly.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COVER OPEN FRACTURES: If bone is visible, cover loosely with the cleanest damp cloth.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Treat as a wound with high infection risk.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: ELEVATE THE LIMB: If possible, rest the limb elevated above heart level to reduce swelling.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE: Open fractures require surgical cleaning within hours to prevent bone infection (osteomyelitis).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Gunshot Wounds Source: TCCC Guidelines (COTCCC 2023); Prehospital Trauma Life Support (PHTLS), 9th Edition; Borden Institute Emergency War Surgery Handbook.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Gunshot wounds (GSW) cause damage along the bullet's path and often beyond it due to the pressure wave.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:25
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Most deaths from GSW are due to bleeding.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:26
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The priority is always: STOP THE BLEEDING.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14:27
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_14
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The MARCH Protocol Follow This Order MARCH is the standard field casualty care sequence used by military medics worldwide.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: the bullet's path and often beyond it due to the pressure wave.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Most deaths from GSW are due to bleeding.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The priority is always: STOP THE BLEEDING.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The MARCH Protocol Follow This Order MARCH is the standard field casualty care sequence used by military medics worldwide.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Use it for every gunshot victim.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Step Action M Massive Hemorrhage Stop all life-threatening bleeding first, before anything else A Airway Ensure the person can breathe; open and clear the airway R Respiration Check and treat chest injuries C Circulation Treat shock; keep them warm and horizontal H Hypothermia Prevent heat loss; cover immediately 3B.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Massive Hemorrhage Stop the Bleeding 121.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DIRECT PRESSURE: Press hard on the wound with the cleanest material available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Press as hard as you physically can.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: WOUND PACKING: For bullet holes push clean cloth deep into the wound with your fingers.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TOURNIQUET: For arm or leg wounds with uncontrollable bleeding, apply improvised tourniquet (see Section 2C).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Apply HIGH and TIGHT as close to the armpit or groin as possible.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: JUNCTIONAL WOUNDS (groin, armpit, neck): These areas cannot be tourniqueted.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Apply direct pressure with your full body weight.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Junctional wounds (where the limb meets the body groin, armpit) are extremely dangerous and cannot have a tourniquet applied.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Constant manual pressure is the only field option.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Airway Ensure They Can Breathe 125.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If conscious and talking: their airway is open.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If unconscious: tilt the head back gently and lift the chin up.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Sweep the mouth with a finger: remove blood, vomit, teeth, or debris.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Turn them on their side (recovery position) if they are breathing but unconscious, to prevent choking on blood or vomit.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Head Gunshot Wound Head wounds bleed profusely even when not life-threatening.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Assess consciousness immediately.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Apply gentle direct pressure to scalp wounds do NOT press hard on skull wounds where the bone may be damaged If unconscious but breathing: recovery position (on side), clear airway Do NOT remove any object embedded in the skull Do NOT give anything to eat or drink Speak calmly even if they appear unconscious hearing may remain Protect from heat and cold Evacuate immediately any loss of consciousness after head GSW requires urgent care 3E.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_15
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Abdominal Gunshot Wound Abdominal GSW

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Do NOT remove any object embedded in the skull Do NOT give anything to eat or drink Speak calmly even if they appear unconscious hearing may remain Protect from heat and cold Evacuate immediately any loss of consciousness after head GSW requires urgent care 3E.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Abdominal Gunshot Wound Abdominal GSW causes internal bleeding that cannot be controlled in the field.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: The only treatment is surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS OF ABDOMINAL GSW Entry wound on abdomen, back, or flank Belly becomes rigid and painful over time Intestines or tissue visible through the wound Signs of shock: pale, sweating, rapid weak pulse, confusion FIELD CARE 129.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT push protruding organs back in.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Cover them with the cleanest damp cloth available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT remove any object from the abdomen.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Apply a large loose dressing over the wound do not pack tightly.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If they are more comfortable with knees bent, allow it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Give nothing by mouth no water, no food.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE URGENTLY internal abdominal bleeding is fatal without surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is a transport priority.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Treating Shock Shock is the body's response to losing too much blood.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: It is a medical emergency.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Sign of Shock Severity Anxious, slightly pale, thirsty Early act now Pale, sweating, confused, rapid pulse Moderate urgent Unresponsive, barely breathing, no pulse at Severe critical wrist Field Treatment for Shock 136.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Raise legs 30 cm if no spinal injury suspected.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Keep them warm cover with everything available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If conscious and not abdominal GSW: small sips of water or oral rehydration salts.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Reassess pulse every 5 minutes.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Blast Injuries / Explosion Source: TCCC Guidelines; NATO Emergency War Surgery (4th Edition); Blast Injury Research Program, US Army Medical Research.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Explosions cause four distinct types of injury that can all occur in the same person simultaneously.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is what makes blast injury more complex than a single wound.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Blast Injury Type What It Means Primary pressure wave Invisible wave of pressure damages lungs, eardrums, bowel, and sinuses Secondary fragments Shrapnel and debris cause penetrating wounds (see Section 2) Tertiary thrown Person is thrown through the air, causing fractures and crush injuries Quaternary burns/crush Burns, building collapse, toxic gas inhalation 4A.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_16
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Immediate Scene Actions Do NOT rush

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: wave Invisible wave of pressure damages lungs, eardrums, bowel, and sinuses Secondary fragments Shrapnel and debris cause penetrating wounds (see Section 2) Tertiary thrown Person is thrown through the air, causing fractures and crush injuries Quaternary burns/crush Burns, building collapse, toxic gas inhalation 4A.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Immediate Scene Actions Do NOT rush to victims immediately after an explosion.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Secondary devices (second bombs placed to target rescuers) are common in conflict zones.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Wait 60 seconds and scan the area before approaching.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: ENSURE SCENE IS SAFE: Scan for fire, structural collapse risk, gas leaks (smell), and secondary threats.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TRIAGE IF MULTIPLE VICTIMS: Quickly walk through and identify who is walking (minor), who is on the ground but breathing (urgent), who is not moving and not breathing (critical/expectant).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CALL FOR HELP: Send someone to get any available medical assistance while you begin care.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Primary Blast Lung Injury The pressure wave can rupture the tiny air sacs in the lungs without any external wound.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is called blast lung and may not be obvious immediately it can worsen over hours.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS MAY APPEAR WITHIN MINUTES TO HOURS AFTER BLAST Coughing up blood or pink foamy sputum Shortness of breath that worsens over time [Page 24] Chest pain, especially when breathing deeply The person was close to the blast even if they appear fine Low oxygen: lips, fingernails, or gums turn blue FIELD CARE 145.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Sit the person upright do not lay flat if they have breathing difficulty 146.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Keep them calm and still exertion worsens blast lung 147.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Monitor breathing closely.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Count breaths per minute (normal is 1220) 148.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If they have both blast lung AND a chest wound: treat the chest wound first (see 2D) 149.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Evacuate: blast lung can become fatal within hours 4C.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Blast Ear Injury (Ruptured Eardrum) The eardrum ruptures under blast pressure.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is extremely common and usually not life- threatening, but the person may be disoriented.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Signs: ringing in ears, hearing loss, pain, blood from ear canal, dizziness Cover the ear loosely with clean cloth do not insert anything into the ear canal Do NOT irrigate or flush the ear A person with blast ear injury may not be able to follow verbal instructions use hand signals and touch Most ruptures heal on their own but require medical assessment to rule out deeper injury 4D.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_17
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Traumatic Amputation from Blast High-order blasts can cause partial or complete

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: or flush the ear A person with blast ear injury may not be able to follow verbal instructions use hand signals and touch Most ruptures heal on their own but require medical assessment to rule out deeper injury 4D.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Traumatic Amputation from Blast High-order blasts can cause partial or complete traumatic amputation of limbs.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TOURNIQUET IMMEDIATELY: Apply as high on the limb as possible before doing anything else.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: A traumatic amputation will bleed fatally within minutes.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: PACK THE STUMP: If the tourniquet does not fully control bleeding, pack clean cloth tightly into the wound and press hard.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT try to reattach or preserve the amputated part in field conditions without ice focus entirely on keeping the person alive.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TREAT FOR SHOCK: Lay flat, keep warm, elevate legs.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Building Collapse / Crush Injury If a person has been trapped under rubble or a heavy object for more than 15 minutes, releasing them can trigger a dangerous reaction called crush syndrome, where toxins released from damaged muscle can cause heart failure.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If a person has been trapped for more than 15 minutes under heavy weight, DO NOT move them without medical guidance if any is available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Releasing the pressure too quickly without IV fluids can cause sudden cardiac arrest.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If you MUST move them: move quickly and be prepared for sudden collapse Lay them flat immediately after extraction Encourage drinking large amounts of water if conscious Look for swollen, hard, dark limbs sign of crush injury Evacuate urgently crush syndrome requires hospital treatment 4F.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Burns from Blast Source: WHO Burns Management; ICRC War Surgery.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Burn Severity What it looks like Minor (1st degree) Red, painful skin, like a sunburn.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Moderate (2nd degree) Blisters, very painful, wet-looking skin Severe (3rd degree) White, brown, or black leathery skin.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Field Treatment for Burns 155.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COOL THE BURN: Pour cool (not ice cold) water over the burn for 1020 minutes.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is the only burn first aid that changes outcomes.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COVER: After cooling, cover loosely with clean dry material.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT: burst blisters, apply toothpaste, oil, butter, or any home remedy these cause infection and make burns worse.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT remove clothing stuck to a burn cut around it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_18
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: FACE BURNS: If eyebrows are singed and the person has a

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT: burst blisters, apply toothpaste, oil, butter, or any home remedy these cause infection and make burns worse.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT remove clothing stuck to a burn cut around it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: FACE BURNS: If eyebrows are singed and the person has a hoarse voice or difficulty swallowing, the airway may be burned internally.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is a critical emergency requiring immediate evacuation.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: TREAT FOR SHOCK: Severe burns cause massive fluid loss and shock.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Airway & Breathing Emergencies Source: TCCC Guidelines; WHO Basic Emergency Care (BEC); American Heart Association CPR Guidelines (2020); Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) 10th Edition.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Airway and breathing emergencies are the most rapidly fatal conditions.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Without oxygen, brain damage begins in 4 minutes and death follows within 10.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: These must be treated before any other injury except massive bleeding.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Assess Breathing Do This First for Every Patient 161.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: LOOK: Is the chest rising and falling?

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: LISTEN: Put your ear near the mouth and nose.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Can you hear breath sounds?

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: FEEL: Can you feel air against your cheek?

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Finding Action Breathing normally Go to next priority bleeding, wounds Breathing noisily (gurgling, snoring) Clear airway see 5B Breathing very fast (>30 per min) Suspect chest injury see Section 2D or 4B Not breathing Begin rescue breaths immediately see 5C Not breathing, no pulse Begin CPR see 5D 5B.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Opening and Clearing the Airway If the person is unconscious: 164.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: HEAD TILT-CHIN LIFT: Place one hand on the forehead, two fingers under the chin.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Tilt head back and lift chin.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This straightens the airway.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If spinal injury is suspected (fall, blast threw them, neck pain mentioned): use JAW THRUST instead place fingers behind the jaw angle and push the jaw forward without tilting the head.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SWEEP THE MOUTH: Use your finger to clear blood, vomit, broken teeth, or debris from the mouth.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Only sweep what you can see.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RECOVERY POSITION: If breathing has returned turn them on their side so vomit drains out and the tongue cannot block the airway.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Airway Blocked by a Solid Object Conscious Adult 168.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Ask: 'Are you choking?' If they cannot speak or cough, they need help.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:25
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: BACK BLOWS: Give 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19:26
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_19
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: ABDOMINAL THRUSTS (Heimlich): Stand behind them, place one fist above the

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: a Solid Object Conscious Adult 168.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Ask: 'Are you choking?' If they cannot speak or cough, they need help.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: BACK BLOWS: Give 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: ABDOMINAL THRUSTS (Heimlich): Stand behind them, place one fist above the navel below the breastbone, cover with other hand, and give 5 sharp upward thrusts.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or the person becomes unconscious.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If unconscious: begin CPR each time you open the airway to give a breath, look in the mouth for the object.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: For pregnant women or people who are very obese: use chest thrusts (same position but hands on the center of the chest) instead of abdominal thrusts.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Rescue Breathing Person Not Breathing, Has Pulse 173.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Tilt head back, lift chin.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Take a normal breath, seal your lips completely around their mouth.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Breathe in gently just enough to see the chest rise (about 1 second).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Give 1 breath every 56 seconds (about 1012 breaths per minute).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Check for pulse every 2 minutes.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If you cannot or will not do mouth-to-mouth: covering the face with a thin cloth allows breath to pass through while reducing direct contact.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CPR No Breathing and No Pulse CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) keeps blood and oxygen circulating when the heart has stopped.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Even imperfect CPR dramatically improves survival.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CPR STEPS ADULTS AND CHILDREN OVER 8 YEARS 179.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: POSITION: Lay the person on their back on a firm surface.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:18
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: HEEL OF HAND: Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest (lower half of the breastbone).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:19
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Place the other hand on top and interlock fingers.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:20
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: COMPRESS: Push straight down firmly and fast at least 56 cm (2 inches).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:21
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Let the chest fully rebound after each compression.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:22
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Do not lean on the chest between compressions.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:23
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RATE: 100120 compressions per minute.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:24
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This is faster than one per second think of the rhythm of a fast song beat.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:25
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RATIO: Give 30 compressions, then 2 rescue breaths.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:26
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If you cannot or will not give rescue breaths: give continuous chest compressions only at 100120 per minute without stopping.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20:27
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_20
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Continue until: the person wakes up, starts breathing, medical

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: rhythm of a fast song beat.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RATIO: Give 30 compressions, then 2 rescue breaths.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If you cannot or will not give rescue breaths: give continuous chest compressions only at 100120 per minute without stopping.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Continue until: the person wakes up, starts breathing, medical help arrives, or you are physically unable to continue.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CPR for Infants (Under 1 Year) Use 2 fingers (middle and ring finger) on the center of the chest, just below the nipple line Compress about 4 cm (1.5 inches) 30 compressions to 2 gentle puffs (cover mouth AND nose together) 100120 compressions per minute CPR for Children (18 Years) Use the heel of one hand only Compress 5 cm (2 inches) 30 compressions to 2 rescue breaths CPR on a person who still has a heartbeat can cause heart problems.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Only begin CPR if you are certain there is no pulse.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Choking on Blood Trauma Airway In trauma, the airway is often blocked by blood rather than a foreign object.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:7
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: This requires different management.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:8
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: DO NOT do abdominal thrusts there is no solid object to dislodge.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:9
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: ROLL ON SIDE: Turn the person onto their side so blood drains out of the mouth by gravity.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:10
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: CLEAR WITH FINGER: If a blood clot is visible in the mouth, sweep it out with your finger.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:11
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SUCTION: If a suction device is available, use it.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:12
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: If a neck or jaw wound is causing airway obstruction and the person is rapidly deteriorating, push the jaw forward and hold it there this lifts the tongue off the airway.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:13
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Tension Pneumothorax Air Trapped in Chest This is one of the most rapidly fatal conditions after trauma.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:14
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: It occurs when air builds up inside the chest cavity (from a lung wound or blast) and compresses the heart and remaining lung.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:15
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: SIGNS THE PERSON IS DETERIORATING DESPITE TREATMENT [Page 29] Breathing becomes extremely difficult and rapid Neck veins bulge visibly The trachea (windpipe) shifts away from center of the neck Blood pressure collapses person becomes unresponsive This occurs after a chest wound has been sealed FIELD ACTION 191.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:16
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RELEASE THE SEAL: If a chest wound has been sealed (see 2D), lift the seal for 23 seconds to allow trapped air to escape.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21:17
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_21
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: POSITION: Sit upright if possible.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:0
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: person becomes unresponsive This occurs after a chest wound has been sealed FIELD ACTION 191.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: RELEASE THE SEAL: If a chest wound has been sealed (see 2D), lift the seal for 23 seconds to allow trapped air to escape.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: POSITION: Sit upright if possible.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:3
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: EVACUATE: This requires needle decompression (a medical procedure).

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:4
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: There is no improvised treatment.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:5
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Rapid evacuation is the only field option.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22:6
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_22
source: field_emergency_guide_v2

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_23:1
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_23
source: field_emergency_guide_v2
text: Every condition described here requires professional medical care as soon as it is available.

id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_23:2
chunk_id: field_emergency_guide_v2_chunk_23

text: Do not delay evacuation to complete field care when evacuation is possible.

text: [Page 1] GENERAL FIRST AID GUIDE For Everyday Civilians Standard Household First Aid Kit Assumed Use Immediately While Awaiting Emergency Medical Services (EMS) REFERENCES: American Heart Association (AHA) American Red Cross WHO First Aid Guidelines Red Cross/Red Crescent International Guidelines n THIS GUIDE IS FOR EMERGENCY REFERENCE ONLY.

id: First_Aid_Guide_chunk_0:1
chunk_id: First_Aid_Guide_chunk_0

text: Call EMS (911 or local emergency number) as soon as possible.
