chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_27
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Another alternative therapy thought by some to boost immune systems and treat illness is colloidal silver.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_27:4

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_27
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_27:6

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_27:8

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This means that, if you are uncertain whether a limb is injured or deformed, you can compare it with the other side.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The strength on each side should be about equal.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These are just some basics.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Certainly, theres a lot more to a physical exam than we just described, but practicing exams on others will give you experience.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As time goes by, youll get the feel of what is normal and what isnt.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: THE MASS CASUALTY INCIDENT Youve just read about performing a physical exam.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most of these exams will be unhurried and routine, but, occasionally, you will have to make some quick decisions.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For major trauma, it is important to take note of the golden hourthe first hour after the victims injury, when his or her chance of survival is highest.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A victims chance of survival decreases significantly if not treated within that hour.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It then worsens with every thirty minutes that pass without care.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Usually, the healthcare provider will be dealing with one ill or injured individual at a time.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There may be a day, however, when you find yourself confronted with an emergency scenario in which multiple people are injured.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is referred to as a mass casualty incident (MCI).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A mass casualty incident is any event in which your medical resources are inadequate for the number and severity of injuries incurred.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: MCIs can be quite variable in their presentation and can include any of the following: Doomsday scenario events, such as nuclear weapon detonations Terrorist acts, such as occurred on 9/11 or in Oklahoma City Consequences of a storm, such as a tornado or hurricane Consequences of civil unrest A mass transit mishap (train derailment, plane crash, etc.) A car accident with, for example, three people significantly injured and only one ambulance The effective medical management of any of the events listed above requires rapid and accurate triage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Triage, which comes from the French word trier (to sort), is the process by which medical personnel can rapidly assess and prioritize a number of injured individuals, thereby doing the most good for the most people.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_31
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Note that I didnt say, Give the best possible care to each individual

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Evaluating an MCI Scene Your initial actions at the scene of an MCI may determine the outcome of the emergency response.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The following constitute the five Ss of evaluating an MCI scene: [Page 26] Safety Sizing up Sending for help Setup of areas Simple triage and rapid treatment (START), a term used in triage 1.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In the Middle East, an insidious strategy on the part of terrorists is the use of primary and secondary bombs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The main bomb causes the most casualties, and the second bomb is timed to go off or is triggered just as the medical and security personnel arrive.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many medical professionals wince when I talk about not approaching the injured in a hostile setting.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Remember that your primary goal as medic is your own self-preservation; keeping the medical personnel alive is likely to save more lives down the road.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As you arrive on the scene, be as certain as possible that there is no ongoing threat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Do not rush in there until it is clear that you and your helpers are safe.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ask yourself the following questions: Whats the situation?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Is this a mass-transit crash?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Did a building on fire collapse?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: How many injuries and how severe?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Are there a few victims or dozens?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Are there others who can help?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Are the victims all together or spread out over a wide area?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: What are possible nearby areas for transport and treatment of the injured?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Are there areas open enough for vehicles to come through to help transport victims?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If modern medical care is available, call 911 and say (for example), I am calling to report a mass casualty incident involving a multivehicle auto accident at the intersection of Hollywood and Vine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: At least seven people are injured and will require medical attention.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There may be people trapped in their cars, and one vehicle is on fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_32

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:1

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There may be people trapped in their cars, and one vehicle is on fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In three sentences, you have informed the authorities that a mass casualty event has occurred, what type of event it was, where it occurred, an approximate number of patients that may need care, and the types of care or equipment that may be needed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you are the only one there, get your phone or other communication device and notify others of the situation and what youll need in terms of personnel and supplies.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you are not medically trained, contact the person who is the group medic.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most experienced medical person is the incident commander.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Determine likely areas for victims of various levels of illness (see below) to be further evaluated and treated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Also, determine the appropriate entry and exit points for victims that need immediate transport to medical facilities, if they exist.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The first round of triage, known as primary triage, should be fast (30 seconds per patient, if possible) and does not involve extensive treatment of injuries.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It should be focused on identifying the triage level of each patient.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Evaluation in primary triage consists mostly of quick evaluation of respiration (or the lack thereof), perfusion (adequacy of circulation), and mental status.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Other than controlling massive bleeding and clearing airways, very little treatment is [Page 27] performed in primary triage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although there is no international standard for this, triage levels are usually determined by color: Immediate (red tag) The victim needs immediate medical care and will not survive without rapid treatment (for example, a major hemorrhagic wound or internal bleeding).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This person has top priority.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Delayed (yellow tag) The victim needs medical care within 24 hours.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Injuries may become life threatening if ignored (for example, open fracture of femur without major hemorrhage) but can wait until patients with red tags are treated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Minimal (green tag)Generally stable and ambulatory (walking wounded) but may need some medical care (for example, broken fingers, sprained wrist).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Expectant (black tag)The victim is either deceased or is not expected to live (for example, open skull fracture with brain damage, or multiple penetrating chest wounds).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_33
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Knowing this patient marking system easily enables a caregiver to understand the urgency of a patients situation.

text: It should go without saying that, in a power-down situation without modern medical care, a lot

text: not expected to live (for example, open skull fracture with brain damage, or multiple penetrating chest wounds).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It will be difficult to save someone with major internal bleeding without surgical intervention.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Lets go through an example of a mass casualty incident and discuss how triage duties should be performed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Primary Triage: MCI Scenario Heres our hypothetical scenario: You are walking down the street when you hear an explosion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You are the first one to arrive at the scene, and you are alone.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are about twenty people down, and there is blood everywhere.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Referring back to the five Ss, lets assume that you have already determined the safety of the current situation and sized-up the scene.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There appears to have been a bomb that exploded.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are no hostiles nearby, as far as you can tell, and there is no evidence of incoming ordnance.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, you believe that you and other responders are not in danger.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The injuries are significant, and the victims are all in one area.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The incident occurred on a main thoroughfare, so there are ways in and out.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You have sent a call for help and described the scene, and have received replies from several group members, including a former intensive care unit (ICU) nurse who is contacting everyone else with medical experience.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_34
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Two bruised but sturdy individuals join you.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: By communicating, you have made your job as temporary incident commander easier by identifying the walking wounded (green tags) and getting some immediate help.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You still have ten victims down.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You then go to the closest victim on the ground.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Start right where you are and go to the next nearest victim in turn.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this way, you will triage faster and more effectively than trying to figure out who needs help the most from a distance or going in a haphazard pattern.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Lets cheat just a little and say that you happen to have what are known as SMART tags in your pack.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: SMART tags are handy tickets that enable you to mark a particular triage level on a patient.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once you identify a victims triage level, you remove a portion of the end of the tag until you reach the appropriate color and place it around the patients wrist.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You could, instead, use colored markers or numbers placed on the victims foreheads.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you use numbers, follow this coding: Priority 1immediate/red Priority 2delayed/yellow Priority 3minimal/green Priority 4dead or expectant/black It is important to remember that you are triaging, not treating.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The only treatments in START will be stopping massive bleeding, opening airways, and elevating the legs in case of shock.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As you go from patient to patient, stay calm, and identify who you are and that youre there to help.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Your goal is to find out who will need help most urgently (red tags).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You will be assessing respiration, perfusion, and mental status (RPM).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Respiration: Is your patient breathing?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If not, tilt the head back or insert an oral airway if available.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Note: In modern emergency care, the neck is not moved unless a cervical spine injury has been ruled out; in an MCI triage situation, the rule is temporarily suspended.) If you have an open airway and no breathing, that victim is tagged black.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the victim breathes once an airway is restored or is breathing more than 30 times a minute, tag red.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the victim is breathing normally, move to perfusion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_35
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Perfusion: Determine how normal the blood flow or circulation is.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It will go from white to normal color in less than 2 seconds if there is good perfusion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36:7

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If there is no pulse, or it takes longer than 2 seconds for the color to return to pink, tag red.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Mental status: Can the patient follow simple commands (open your eyes, whats your name?)?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tag patients yellow if they can understand you and follow commands but cant get up, green if they can.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Remember that, as a consequence of the explosion, some [Page 29] victims may not be able to hear you well.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It might be easier to remember all this by just thinking 302Can Do: 30 (respirations), 2 (CRT), Can Do (Commands).

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once you have identified someone as triage level red, tag them and move immediately to the next patient unless you have major bleeding to stop.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_36
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For example, if someone wasnt breathing but began breathing once you repositioned the airway, tag red, and stop further evaluation if the person is not hemorrhaging.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When you eat, these bacterial colonies also have a meal; they digest the sugars you take in and [Page 38] produce a toxic acid.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This acid has the effect of slowly dissolving the enamel of your teeth.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once the enamel has broken down, a cavity is created.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When the cavity becomes deep enough to invade the soft inner part of the tooth (the pulp), the process speeds up and, because you have living nerves in each tooth, starts to cause pain.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the cavity isnt dealt with, it can lead to infection once the bacteria dig deep enough into the nerve or the surrounding gum tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Inflamed gums have a distinctive appearance: Theyll appear red and swollen; theyll bleed when you brush your teeth.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Known as gingivitis, this is very common in adults.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the condition worsens, it can easily lead to infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If it affects the gums, it may spread to the roots of teeth or even the bony socket.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once the root of the tooth is involved, you could develop a particularly severe infection (abscess).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is an accumulation of pus and inflammatory fluid that causes gum swelling and can be quite painful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once you have an abscess, you will need antibiotic therapy and, perhaps, a procedure to drain the pus that has accumulated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_49
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The tooth will likely be unsalvageable at this point.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A dental mirror and dental pick are good tools to start with.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If there is nothing that you can see, however, you may still have serious decay between teeth or below the gums.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_50:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_50
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_50
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_50:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_50
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A tooth that is probably beyond hope will cause significant pain when you touch it with something hot (only touch the tooth).

text: The goal of modern dentistry is to save every tooth, if at all possible.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: After an injury to the oral cavity, a person may have any of the following: Dental fractureportion of a tooth chipped or broken off Dental subluxationa loose tooth Dental avulsiona tooth knocked out completely [Page 40] When a portion of a tooth is broken off, it is categorized on the basis of the number of layers of the tooth that are exposed.

text: Dentists generally refer to these as Ellis class I, II, or III fractures: Ellis I fracture: This is where only the enamel has been broken and no dentin or pulp is exposed.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_54
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Flush the tooth clean of dirt and debris with water or saline solution.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_54:10

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_55

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS Even with todays modern medical technology, most of us cant avoid the occasional respiratory infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_57:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_57
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS Even with todays modern medical technology, most of us cant avoid the occasional respiratory infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without strict adherence to sanitary protocol, it would be very easy in a major disaster for your entire community to come down with colds, sinusitis, influenza, or even pneumonia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Common colds may be caused by any of 200 different viruses.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Influenza comes from viruses in the Influenza A, B, and C categories (mostly A).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Over the course of history, influenza outbreaks have killed more than 100 million people.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: [Page 44] Most of the deaths associated with influenza are not caused by the virus itself, but instead by bacterial pneumonia, a secondary infection that invades a virus-weakened immune system.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In general, most respiratory infections are spread by viral particles, and many organisms that cause these infections can live for up to 48 hours on common household surfaces, such as kitchen counters and doorknobs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Contagious viral particles can easily travel 46 feet when a person sneezes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Respiratory issues are usually divided into upper and lower respiratory infections.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The upper respiratory tract is considered to be anything at the level of the vocal cords (larynx) or above.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The diagnosis often will be related to the affected part of the upper respiratory system.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Heres how it works: noserhinitis throatpharyngitis sinusessinusitis voice boxlaryngitis epiglottisepiglottitis tonsilstonsillitis ear canalotitis The lower respiratory tract includes the lower windpipe, the airways (taken together, called bronchi), and the lungs themselves.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Respiratory infections, such as bronchitis and pneumonia, are the most common cause of infectious disease in developed countries.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Typical N95 mask Symptoms of the common cold can include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, nasal congestion, headaches, and sneezing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Symptoms of lower respiratory infections (pneumonia and some bronchitis) include cough (with phlegm, a productive cough), high fever, shortness of breath, weakness, and fatigue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most respiratory infections start showing symptoms 13 days after exposure to the causative organism.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They can be expected to last 710 days if upper and somewhat longer if lower.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Influenza There are differences between the common cold and influenza that are helpful to know in making a diagnosis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The symptoms are similar but differ in frequency and severity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_58
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Consult the list below to identify what youre most likely dealing with: Symptoms Cold Influenza Fever Rare, Low Common, High Headache Rare Common Nasal congestion Common Occasional Sore throat Common Occasional Cough Mild Severe Aches and pains Common Severe

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The symptoms are similar but differ in frequency and severity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Consult the list below to identify what youre most likely dealing with: Symptoms Cold Influenza Fever Rare, Low Common, High Headache Rare Common Nasal congestion Common Occasional Sore throat Common Occasional Cough Mild Severe Aches and pains Common Severe Fatigue Mild Severe For influenza, the administration of antiviral medications such as oseltamivir (TamifluTM) will shorten the course of the infection if taken in the first 48 hours after symptoms appear.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: After the first 48 hours, antivirals have less medicinal effect.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For colds, concentrate your treatment on the area involved: nasal congestion medication for runny noses or sore throat lozenges for pharyngitis, for example.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ibuprofen or [Page 45] acetaminophen will alleviate muscle aches and fevers.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Steam inhalation and good hydration also give some symptomatic relief.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Various natural remedies are also useful to relieve symptoms, which we discuss in the next section of this book.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although most upper respiratory infections are caused by viruses, some sore throats may be caused by a bacterium called beta Streptococcus (strep throat).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These patients will often have small white spots on the back of their throat, tonsils, or both and are candidates for antibiotics.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Amoxicillin (veterinary equivalent: Fish Mox) or Keflex (Fish Flex) are included among the drugs of choice in those not allergic to penicillin drugs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Erythromycin (Fish Mycin) family drugs are helpful in those who are penicillin-allergic.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In most cases, however, it is not appropriate to use antibacterial agents such as antibiotics for upper respiratory infections.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Antibiotics have been overused in treating these problems, and this has led to resistance on the part of some organisms to the more common drugs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Resistance has rendered some of the older antibiotics almost useless in the treatment of many illnesses.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Lower respiratory infections, such as pneumonia, are the most common cause of death from infectious disease in developed countries.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These can be caused by viruses or bacteria.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The more serious nature of these infections leads many practitioners to use antibiotics more often to treat the condition.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most bronchitis is caused by viruses, however, and will not be affected by antibiotics.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Antibiotics may be appropriate for those with a lower respiratory infection that hasnt improved after several days of treatment with the usual medications for upper respiratory infections.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_59
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patients who are at risk will appear to have worsening shortness of breath or thicker phlegm over the

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: be affected by antibiotics.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Antibiotics may be appropriate for those with a lower respiratory infection that hasnt improved after several days of treatment with the usual medications for upper respiratory infections.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patients who are at risk will appear to have worsening shortness of breath or thicker phlegm over the course of time despite the usual therapy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Both upper and lower respiratory infections are different from asthma, a condition where the airways become constricted in a type of spasm when exposed to a substance.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This causes a particularly vocal kind of breathing (wheeze).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Asthma may occur as an allergic response, or may be associated with some respiratory infections, such as childhood croup.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The treatment of asthma involves different medicines not used with colds or flus, such as airway openers and epinephrine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Good respiratory hygiene is important to prevent patients with respiratory infections from transmitting their infection to others.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is not only a good strategy for you and your family, but demonstrates social responsibility.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use the protocols below to prevent the spread of respiratory infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sick individuals: Cover mouth and nose with tissues and dispose of those tissues safely.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use a mask if coughing often.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although others caring for the sick individual may wear masks (N95 masks are best for healthcare providers), it is most important for [Page 46] the afflicted person to wear one.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_60:13

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diarrhea is a common ailment that may go away on its own simply by restricting your patient to clear fluids and avoiding solid food for 12 hours.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_69
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: However, the following symptoms that may present in association with diarrhea can be a sign of something more serious: Fever equal to or greater than 101 degrees Blood or mucus in the stool Black or grey-white stool Severe vomiting Major abdominal distension and pain Moderate to severe dehydration Diarrhea lasting more than 3 days All of these symptoms may be signs of serious infection, intestinal bleeding, liver dysfunction, or even conditions that require surgery, such as appendicitis.
