id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: One relatively common issue that could be life threatening in a long-term survival situation, especially to young people, would be appendicitis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Appendicitis (inflammation of the appendix) occurs in approximately 8 out of every 100 people.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Appendicitis can occur in anyone but most likely affects people under forty.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The appendix is a tubular, worm-shaped piece of tissue 24 inches long that connects to the intestine at the lower right side of the abdomen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The inside of this structure forms a pouch that opens [Page 55] to the large intestine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The purpose of the appendix is unknown, but one theory is that it is an example of a vestigial organ, which means that it is a useless remnant from our evolutionary past that now serves little useful purpose.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The appendix causes trouble when it is blocked or bacteria are passed along from elsewhere in the body.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The bacteria can multiply and cause inflammation or infection, and even cause the appendix to fill up with pus.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the problem is not treated, the appendix can burst, spilling infected matter into the abdominal cavity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This causes peritonitis, a condition that can spread throughout the entire abdomen and become very serious.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Before the development of antibiotics, it was not unusual to die from the infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Appendicitis starts off with vague discomfort in the area of the belly button but moves down to the lower right quadrant of the abdomen after 1224 hours.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This area, also known as McBurneys Point, is located about two-thirds of the way down from the belly button to the top of the right pelvic bone.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Other likely symptoms may include the following: Nausea and vomiting Loss of appetite Fever and chills Abdominal swelling Pain worsening with coughs or walking Difficulty passing gas Constipation or diarrhea A patient may resist using his or her legs, because that triggers movement of abdominal muscles.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Nausea, vomiting, and fever are other common signs and symptoms of appendicitis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: To diagnose this condition, press down on the lower right of the abdomen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Your patient will probably find it painful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A sign of a possible ruptured appendix may be what is called rebound tenderness.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this circumstance, pressing down will cause pain, but it will be even more painful when you remove your hand.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_72
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient should be restricted to small amounts of clear liquids as soon as you make the diagnosis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: ruptured appendix may be what is called rebound tenderness.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this circumstance, pressing down will cause pain, but it will be even more painful when you remove your hand.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient should be restricted to small amounts of clear liquids as soon as you make the diagnosis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Surgical removal of the appendix is curative here but will be difficult to carry out without modern medical facilities.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If modern surgical care is unavailable, your only hope may be giving the patient antibiotics by mouth in the hope of eliminating an early infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Of course, intravenous antibiotics, such as cefoxitin, are more effective than related oral antibiotics, such as cephalexin (veterinary equivalent: Fish Flex).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Studies in the United Kingdom achieved some success using intravenous antibiotics in early (uncomplicated) cases of appendicitis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A combination of ciprofloxacin (veterinary equivalent: Fish Cin) and metronidazole (Fish Zole) is an option if intravenous antibiotics or surgical intervention is not available.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is also acceptable in those allergic to penicillins.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Recovery, although slow, may still be possible if treatment is begun early enough or the body has formed a wall around the infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: [Page 56] Can surgery be performed in situations where general anesthesia is unavailable?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most surgeries cant, without risking the loss of the patient.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Surgeons in developing countries, however, have done appendectomies under local anesthesia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Before surgery is contemplated to deal with an inflamed appendix, you must be certain that you are dealing with that exact problem.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sometimes, different medical problems present with similar symptoms, and you will have to do some detective work to differentiate one from another.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is called making the differential diagnosis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are various conditions that may mimic appendicitis, including those described below.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tubal Pregnancy In women of childbearing age, a tubal pregnancy should be ruled out.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is a condition that occurs in 1 in every 125 pregnancies.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this condition, a fertilized egg fails to implant in the normal location (the uterine wall) and implants in the fallopian tube instead.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It grows in this tiny canal until it reaches a size that bursts the tube.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This, oftentimes, will cause pain and internal bleeding; in the past, it was not uncommon for a tubal pregnancy to be fatal.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this case, the pain is due to the presence of blood instead of an infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_73
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you have women of childbearing age in your family or survival group, have some pregnancy

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: pain and internal bleeding; in the past, it was not uncommon for a tubal pregnancy to be fatal.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this case, the pain is due to the presence of blood instead of an infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you have women of childbearing age in your family or survival group, have some pregnancy tests in your medical supplies.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A woman with a missed period, positive pregnancy test, and severe pain on one side of the lower abdomen is a tubal pregnancy until proven otherwise.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diverticulitis Diverticulitis, unlike appendicitis, is seen mostly in older patients.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diverticula are small pouches in the large bowel that resemble an inner tube peeking out of a defect in an old-timey car tire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These areas may become blocked just as the appendix might.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The symptoms are very similar, but most diverticulitis patients will complain of pain in the lower left quadrant instead of the right.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Other inflammatory conditions in the bowel, such as Crohns disease or ulcerative colitis, may present with pelvic pain.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These are commonly treated with steroids but may require surgery, as well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease A female pelvic infection often caused by sexually transmitted diseases, such as gonorrhea or chlamydia, may imitate some of the symptoms of an inflamed appendix.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is known as pelvic inflammatory disease (or PID).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These patients will, however, usually have pain on both sides of the lower abdomen, associated with fever and, sometimes, a foul vaginal discharge.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pelvic inflammatory disease can cause major damage to internal female anatomy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Scarring ensues as the body tries to heal, sometimes causing infertility and chronic discomfort.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Serious female infections involving the pelvis are best treated with antibiotics, such as doxycycline, sometimes in combination with metronidazole twice a day for a week.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is a good idea to treat sexual partners, too.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ovarian Cysts [Page 57] Other female issues in the pelvis, such as large or ruptured ovarian cysts, could also cause pain due to pressure or bleeding.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An ovarian cyst is an accumulation of fluid within an ovary that is surrounded by a wall.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many arise from egg follicles, but others can be benign or, less often, cancerous, tumors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most cysts cause pain by rupturing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A rupture may cause a painful irritation of the abdominal lining, internal bleeding, or both.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sometimes, ovarian cysts go away spontaneously, but a ruptured cyst that is actively bleeding will require surgery.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_74
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A right-sided ruptured cyst could appear similar to

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: less often, cancerous, tumors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most cysts cause pain by rupturing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A rupture may cause a painful irritation of the abdominal lining, internal bleeding, or both.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sometimes, ovarian cysts go away spontaneously, but a ruptured cyst that is actively bleeding will require surgery.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A right-sided ruptured cyst could appear similar to appendicitis as the pain is in the same location.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The diagnosis of appendicitis or other causes of abdominal pain without modern diagnostic equipment will be challenging.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Despite this, we have to remember that medical personnel, in the past, had only the physical signs and symptoms to help them reach a diagnosis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS Besides the bowels, bodily waste is excreted through the urinary tract.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The urinary tract includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is, essentially, the bodys plumbing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most women, at some time of their lives, have experienced a urinary tract infection (UTI).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An infection of the bladder (cystitis) usually affects the urethra (the tube that drains the bladder) as well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Various bacteria may cause this infection; Escherichia coli (E.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although men are not immune from a bladder infection, the male urethra is much longer.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, its more difficult for bacteria to reach the bladder.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some urinary infections are sexually transmitted, such as gonorrhea.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In men, painful urination (dysuria) is very common, though most women might only note a yellowish vaginal discharge.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although painful urination is not uncommon in cystitis, the most common symptom is frequency of the need to urinate.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_75:18

text: Conditions that might cause cellulitis include the following: Cracks or peeling skin between the toes Poor circulation, including varicose veins Injuries that cause a break in the skin Insect bites and stings, animal bites, or human bites Ulcers from chronic illness, such as diabetes Use of steroids or other medications that affect the immune system Wounds from previous surgery Intravenous drug use The symptoms and signs of cellulitis are as follows: Discomfort or pain in the area of infection Fever and chills Exhaustion General ill feeling (malaise) Muscle aches (myalgia) Warmth in the area of the infection Drainage of pus or cloudy fluid from the area of the infection Redness, usually spreading towards torso Swelling in the area of infection (causing a sensation of tightness) Foul odor coming from the area of infection Although the body can sometimes resolve cellulitis on its own, treatment usually includes the use of antibiotics.

text: (See how to extract a tooth in the dental section of this book.) Tetanus Classic position associated with tetanus Most of us have dutifully gone to get a tetanus shot when we stepped on a rusty nail, but few have any real concept of what tetanus is and why it is dangerous.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanus is an infection caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The bacteria produces spores (a reproductive cell, or inactive bacteria-to-be) that primarily live in the soil or the feces of animals.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These spores are capable of living for years and are resistant to extremes in temperature.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanus is relatively rare in the United States, with about 50 reported cases a year.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Worldwide, however, there are more than 500,000 cases a year.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most victims are found in developing countries that have poor immunization programs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanus infections usually occur when a person has experienced a break in the skin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The skin is an important barrier to infection, and any chink in the armor leaves a person open to infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most common cause is some type of puncture wound, such as an insect or animal bite, a splinter, or even that rusty nail.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is because the tetanus bacterium doesnt like oxygen, and deep, narrow wounds give less access to it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Any injury that compromises the skin, however, is eligible: Burns, crush injuries, and lacerations can be entryways for tetanus [Page 64] bacteria.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When a wound becomes contaminated with tetanus spores, the spores become activated as full-fledged bacteria and reproduce rapidly.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Damage to the victim comes as a result of a strong toxin excreted by the organism, tetanospasmin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_83
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This toxin specifically targets nerves that serve muscle tissue.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This toxin specifically targets nerves that serve muscle tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanospasmin binds to motor nerves, causing misfires that lead to involuntary contraction of the affected areas.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This neural damage can be localized or affect the entire body.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient may exhibit the classical symptom of lockjaw, where the jaw muscle is taut.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: However, any muscle group is susceptible if affected by the toxin, including the respiratory musculature, which can inhibit normal breathing and become life threatening.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most severe cases seem to occur at extremes of age, with newborns and people older than 65 most likely to succumb to the disease.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Death rates from generalized tetanus hover around 25 50 percent, higher in newborns.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You will be on the lookout for the following early symptoms: Sore muscles (especially near the site of injury) Weakness Irritability Difficulty swallowing Lockjaw Initial symptoms may not present themselves for up to 2 weeks.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the disease progresses, you may see the following: Progressively worsening muscle spasms (may start locally and become generalized over time) Involuntary arching of the back (sometimes so strong that bones may break or dislocations may occur) Fever Respiratory distress High blood pressure Irregular heartbeats The first thing that the survival medic should understand is that, although an infectious disease, Tetanus is not contagious.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can feel confident treating a tetanus victim safely, as long as you wear gloves and observe standard clean technique.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water, using an irrigation syringe to flush out any debris.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This should limit growth of the bacteria and, as a result, decrease toxin production.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You will want to administer antibiotics to kill off the rest of the bacteria in the system.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Administering 500 mg of metronidazole (veterinary equivalent: Fish Zole) 2 times a day or 100 mg of doxycycline (veterinary equivalent: Bird Biotic) 2 times a day is known to be effective.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The earlier you begin antibiotic therapy, the fewer toxins will be produced.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Intravenous rehydration, if you have the ability to administer it, is also helpful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient will be more comfortable in an environment with dim lights and reduced noise.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_84
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ventilators, tetanus antitoxin, and muscle relaxants or sedatives, such

text: The earlier you begin antibiotic therapy, the fewer toxins will be produced.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Intravenous rehydration, if you have the ability to administer it, is also helpful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient will be more comfortable in an environment with dim lights and reduced noise.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ventilators, tetanus antitoxin, and muscle relaxants or sedatives, such as ValiumTM (diazepam), are used to treat severe cases but will be unlikely to be available [Page 65] to you.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For this reason, it is extraordinarily important to watch anyone who has sustained a wound for the early symptoms listed above.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanus can be prevented by vaccination.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Booster injections are usually given every ten years.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tetanus vaccine is not without its risks, but severe complications, such as seizures or brain damage, occur in less than one in a million cases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Milder side effects, such as fatigue, fever, nausea and vomiting, headache, and inflammation in the injection site, are more common.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: MOSQUITO-BORNE ILLNESSES Mosquito bites are common vectors (transmitters) of various infectious diseases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction) as seen with bee stings is rarely an issue with mosquitos and is covered later in this book.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Only female mosquitos bite humans.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The increased amount of time we would spend outside in a survival situation would increase the chances of exposure to one or more mosquito-borne illnesses.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: One of the most notorious diseases caused by mosquito vectors is malaria.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Malaria is caused by a microscopic organism called a protozoan.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When mosquitos bite you, they inject these microbes into your system.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once in the body, the protozoa colonize your liver.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: From there, they go to your blood cells and other organs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Symptoms of malaria appear flu-like, and classically present as periodic chills, fever, and sweats.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patient becomes anemic as more blood cells are damaged by the protozoa.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: With time, periods between episodes become shorter and permanent organ damage may occur.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Anyone that experiences periodic fevers with severe chills and sweating should be considered candidates for treatment.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Medications used for malaria include chloroquine, quinine, and quinidine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sometimes an antibiotic, such as doxycycline or clindamycin, is used in combination with the medications mentioned above.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Physicians are usually sympathetic towards prescribing these medications to those who are contemplating trips to places where mosquitos are rampant.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Other mosquito-borne diseases include yellow fever, dengue fever, and West Nile virus.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_85
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The fewer mosquitos near your retreat, the less likely you will fall victim to one of these diseases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: are usually sympathetic towards prescribing these medications to those who are contemplating trips to places where mosquitos are rampant.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Other mosquito-borne diseases include yellow fever, dengue fever, and West Nile virus.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The fewer mosquitos near your retreat, the less likely you will fall victim to one of these diseases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can decrease the population of mosquitos in your area and improve the likelihood of preventing illness by taking the following precautions: Look for areas of standing water that could serve as mosquito breeding grounds.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Drain all water that you do not depend upon for survival.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Repair any holes or defects in the screens on your retreat windows and doors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Be careful to avoid outside activities at dusk or dawn.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is the time that mosquitos are most active.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wear long pants and shirts whenever you venture outside.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Have a good stockpile of insect repellants.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you are reluctant to use chemical repellants, you may consider natural remedies.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Plants that contain citronella may be rubbed on your skin and clothing to discourage bites.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: [Page 66] When you use an essential oil to repel insects, reapply frequently and feel free to combine oils as needed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Besides citronella oil, you could use the following oils: Lemon eucalyptus Cinnamon Peppermint Geranium Clove Rosemary V.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS A creatures habitat is the place where it lives.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This could be a forest, a lake, or the underside of a leaf.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre a human being, your habitat is likely a town.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When you are in an environment that is not your own, careful planning is necessary to avoid running afoul of the elements.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The focus of your medical training should be general, but also take into account the type of environment that you expect to live in if a disaster occurs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Learn how to treat the likely medical issues for the climate in which youll find yourself.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many aspects of climate can pose risk, especially extremes of ambient temperature.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Humans are susceptible to damage as a result of being too cold or too hot.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The body has various methods it uses to control its internal core temperature, either raising it or lowering it to appropriate levels.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_86:23
