source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For example, you lose more heat if exposed to an outside temperature of 20 degrees than if exposed to 80 degrees.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The body loses heat when its surface is in direct contact with cold temperatures, as in the case of someone falling from a boat into frigid water.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Water, being denser than air, removes heat from the body much faster.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Convection is a form of heat transfer where, for instance, a cooler object is in motion against the body core.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The air next to the skin is heated and then removed, which requires the body to use energy to reheat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wind chill is one example of air convection: If the ambient temperature is 32 degrees, but the wind chill factor is at 5 degrees, you lose heat from your body as if the ambient temperature were actually 5 degrees.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The body, once it is exposed to cold, kicks into action to produce heat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The main mechanism to produce heat is shivering.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Muscles shiver to produce heat, and this will be the first symptom youre likely to see of hypothermia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the condition worsens, more symptoms will become apparent if the patient is not warmed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_90
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Aside from shivering, the most noticeable symptoms of hypothermia will be related to mental status: confusion,

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Muscles shiver to produce heat, and this will be the first symptom youre likely to see of hypothermia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the condition worsens, more symptoms will become apparent if the patient is not warmed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Aside from shivering, the most noticeable symptoms of hypothermia will be related to mental status: confusion, lack of coordination, and lethargy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the condition worsens, speech may become slurred; the patient will appear apathetic and uninterested in helping themselves, or may fall asleep.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This occurs because of the effect of cooling temperatures on the brain: the colder the body core gets, the slower the brain works.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Brain function ceases at about 68 degrees, although I have read of exceptional cases in which people (usually children) have survived even lower temperatures.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Preventing hypothermia means anticipating weather conditions you may encounter and dressing appropriately.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It may be useful to remember the simple acronym COLD, which stands for cover, overexertion, layering, and dry: Cover.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Protect your head by wearing a hat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This will prevent body heat from escaping.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Instead of using gloves to cover your hands, use mittens.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Mittens are more helpful than gloves because they keep your fingers in contact with one another.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid activities that cause you to sweat a lot.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Cold weather causes you to lose body heat quickly, and wet, sweaty clothing accelerates the process.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use regular rest periods to self-assess for cold-related changes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pay careful attention to the status of your elderly, juvenile, or diabetic group members.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Loose-fitting, lightweight clothing in layers insulates you well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use clothing made of tightly woven, water-repellent material for protection against the wind.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wool or [Page 70] silk inner layers hold body heat better than cotton does.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some synthetic materials also work well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Get out of wet clothing as soon as possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its very easy for snow to get into gloves and boots, so pay particular attention to your hands and feet.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Travelers should anticipate the climate they will be traveling through, including wind conditions and wet weather.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They should condition themselves physically to be fit for the challenge, travel with a partner, if at all possible, and have enough food and water available for the entire trip.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: One factor that most people dont take into account is the effect consumption of alcohol can have in cold conditions.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_91
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: While it may give you a warm feeling, alcohol

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: the challenge, travel with a partner, if at all possible, and have enough food and water available for the entire trip.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: One factor that most people dont take into account is the effect consumption of alcohol can have in cold conditions.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: While it may give you a warm feeling, alcohol actually causes your blood vessels to expand, resulting in more-rapid heat loss from the surface of your body.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The body reacts to cold by constricting the blood vessels, so expansion would negate the bodys efforts to stay warm.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Alcohol also causes impaired judgment, which, for example, might cause those under the influence to choose clothing that would not protect them in cold weather.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This also goes for various recreational drugs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you encounter a person in a cold environment who is unconscious, confused or lethargic, you should always assume they are hypothermic until proven otherwise.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Immediate action must be taken to reverse the ill effects of hypothermia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Make sure to do the following: Get the person out of the cold.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre unable to move the person, shield them from the cold and wind as much as possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the person is wearing wet clothing, remove them gently.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Cover them with layers of dry blankets, including the head (leave the face clear).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you are outside, cover the ground to eliminate exposure to the cold surface.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A person with severe hypothermia may be unconscious.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Verify that the patient is breathing and check for a pulse.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: To warm the persons body, remove your clothing and lie next to the person, making skin-to-skin contact.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Then cover both of your bodies with blankets.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some people may cringe at this notion, but its important to remember that you are trying to save a life.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Gentle massage or rubbing may be helpful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the affected person is alert and able to swallow, provide a warm, nonalcoholic, noncaffeinated beverage to help warm the body.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use a dry warm compress and apply only to the neck, chest wall or groin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These areas will spread the heat much better than putting warm compresses on the extremities, which sometimes worsens the condition.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid applying direct heat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont use hot water, a heating pad or a heating lamp to warm the person.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_92
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The extreme heat can damage the skin

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These areas will spread the heat much better than putting warm compresses on the extremities, which sometimes worsens the condition.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid applying direct heat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont use hot water, a heating pad or a heating lamp to warm the person.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The extreme heat can damage the skin and causes strain on the heart.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If left untreated, hypothermia leads to complete failure of various organ systems and to death.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: People who develop hypothermia because of exposure to cold are also vulnerable [Page 71] to other cold- related injuries, such as frostbite and immersion foot.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Frostbite and Immersion (Trench) Foot Frostbite, or the freezing of body tissues, usually occurs in the extremities and sometimes the ears and nose.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Initial symptoms include a pins and needles sensation and numbness.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Skin color changes from red to white to blue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the color then changes to black, gangrene has set in.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Gangrene is the death of tissue resulting from loss of circulation.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This usually results in the loss of the body part affected.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Immersion foot (formerly known as trench foot) causes damage to nerves and small blood vessels from prolonged immersion in water.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This condition appears similar to frostbite but might make the affected foot look more swollen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Frostbite or immersion foot is treated with a warm-water (no more than 104 degrees) soak of the affected extremity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When treating these conditions, keep in mind the following: Dont allow thawed tissue to freeze again.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The more often tissue freezes and thaws, the deeper the damage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you cant prevent your patient from being exposed to freezing temperatures again, you should wait before treating, but not more than a day.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont rub or massage frostbitten tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Rubbing frostbitten tissue will result in damage to already-injured tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont use heat lamps or fires to treat frostbite.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: People with frostbite are numb and cannot feel the frostbitten tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Significant burns can ensue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can use body heat to thaw mild frostbite.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can put mildly frostbitten fingers under your arm, for example, to warm them up.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Cold Water Safety Water doesnt have to be cold to cause hypothermia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Any water thats cooler than normal body temperature will cause heat loss.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_93:27

text: ALTITUDE SICKNESS In any survival situation, we might find ourselves having to relocate from a home at sea level to a retreat in the mountains.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When this becomes necessary, its likely that you will be moving fast.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The rapid change in elevation will, for some, cause altitude sickness, also known as acute mountain sickness (AMS).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This condition occurs as a result of entering an area with lower oxygen availability and reduced air pressures without first acclimating oneself.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: AMS occurs most commonly at elevations approaching 8,000 feet above sea level, and is aggravated by exertion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although it is usually a temporary condition, some patients may develop complications in the form of edema of certain organs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Edema is the accumulation of fluid; in altitude sickness, it may occur in the lungs (pulmonary edema) or brain (cerebral edema).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Either of these conditions can be life threatening.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_95
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Like many illnesses, the best strategy against AMS is prevention.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_96:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_96
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If mild, they commonly include the following: Fatigue Insomnia Dizziness Headaches Nausea and vomiting Lack of appetite Tachycardia (fast heart rate) Pins and needles sensations Shortness of breath In severe cases, you may see the following: Severe shortness of breath Confusion Cough and chest congestion (not nasal) Cyanosis (blue or gray appearance of the skin, especially the fingertips and lips) Loss of coordination Dehydration Hemoptysis (coughing up blood) Loss of consciousness Fever (rare) Treating AMS first requires rest, if only to stop further ascent and allow more time to acclimate.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_96:15

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This might mean [Page 74] that youd have to remove those thorny bushes youve planted under your windows for defense purposes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Have a shelter made of fire-resistant materials.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A wood-frame home with wooden shingles will go up like a match in a wildfire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: So, lets create a defensible spacean area around a structure where wood and vegetation are treated, cleared, or reduced to slow the spread of wildfire towards a structure.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Having a defensible space will also provide room to work for those fighting the fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The amount of defensible space youll need depends on whether youre on flat land or on a steep slope.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Flatland fires spread more slowly than a fire on a slope.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Hot air and flames rise.) A fire on a steep slope with wind blowing uphill will spread quickly and produces spot firessmall fires that ignite vegetation ahead of the main burn because of small bits of burning debris in the air.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Youll want to thin out thick-canopied trees near your house.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This means any nearby tree within 50 feet on flat land or 200 feet if downhill from your retreat.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Prune branches off below 10 12 feet high; trees should be separated by 1020 feet.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Also eliminate all shrubs at the base of the trunks.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Of course, once you have a defensible space, the natural inclination is to want to defend it, even against a forest fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Unfortunately, you have to remember that youll be in the middle of a lot of heat and smoke.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_97
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This would make it difficult unless youre in full fire protection gear.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: once you have a defensible space, the natural inclination is to want to defend it, even against a forest fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Unfortunately, you have to remember that youll be in the middle of a lot of heat and smoke.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This would make it difficult unless youre in full fire protection gear.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The safest option, if theres a way out, would be to leave.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre leaving, have your supplies already in the car, as well as any important papers you might need to keep and some cash.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you have electricity, make sure you shut off any air- conditioning system that draws air into the house from outside.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Turn off all appliances, close all windows, and lock all doors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Let others know where youre going.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If there is any possibility that you might find yourself trapped in a fire, dress in long pants, a long-sleeved shirt, and heavy boots.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A wool blanket is very helpful as an additional outside layer because wool is relatively fire resistant.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre in a building, stay on the side of the building farthest from the fire outside.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Choose a room with the least number of windows.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Windows transfer heat to the inside.) Stay there unless you have to leave because of smoke or the buildings catching fire.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If thats the case, wrap yourself in that blanket, leaving only your eyes uncovered.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some people think its a good idea to wet the blanket first.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wet materials transfer heat much faster than dry materials and will cause more severe burns.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre having trouble breathing because of the smoke, stay low and crawl out of the building if you have to.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Theres less smoke and heat the lower you go.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Keep your face down towards the floor.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This will protect your airway.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont forget to have some eye wash in your supplies, as smoke irritates your eyes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you encounter a person who is actually on fire, you have to act quickly.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In [Page 75] circumstances where a persons clothes are on fire, remember the old adage stop, drop, and roll: Stop.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The victim will be panicked and likely running around trying to put out the flames.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This generates wind, which will fan the flames.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Stop the victim from running away.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Knock the victim to the ground.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:27
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If possible, wrap them in a blanket.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98:28
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_98
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Roll the victim on the ground

text: This generates wind, which will fan the flames.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99

text: If possible, wrap them in a blanket.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Roll the victim on the ground until the flames are extinguished.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Immediately cool any burned areas of skin with water.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Smoke Inhalation Other than burns, which are discussed in another part of this book, you can become seriously ill or even die simply from inhaling too much smoke.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Remember, you can heal from burns on your skin, but you cant heal from burns in your lungs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Common causes of smoke inhalation injury include the following: Simple combustion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Combustion uses up oxygen near a fire and can kill a person simply from oxygen deficit, known as hypoxia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The larger the fire, the more oxygen it removes from the area, especially a closed space.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some byproducts of smoke may not directly kill a person but could take up the space in the lungs that oxygen would ordinarily use.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many chemicals found in smoke can cause irritation injury when they come in contact with the lung.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This amounts to a burn inside the lung tissue, which causes swelling and airway obstruction.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An example from World War I is chlorine gas.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Carbon Monoxide, Cyanide, and some Sulfides may interfere with the bodys ability to use oxygen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Carbon Monoxide is the most common of these.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Symptoms may include the following: Cough Shortness of breath Hoarseness Upper airway spasm Eye irritation Headaches Pale, bluish, or even bright-red skin Loss of consciousness leading to coma or death Your evaluation of the patient with smoke inhalation may show soot around the mouth, in the throat, and in nasal passages.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These areas may be swollen and irritated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The victim will likely be short of breath and have a hoarse voice.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Of course, you will want to get your patient out of the smoky area and into an environment where there is clean air.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You must be very careful not to put yourself in a situation where you are likely to succumb to smoke inhalation yourself.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Always consider a mask before entering a conflagration to rescue a victim.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Be prepared to use CPR if necessary.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_99
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is important to have some way to deliver oxygen to your patient if needed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: to put yourself in a situation where you are likely to succumb to smoke inhalation yourself.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Always consider a mask before entering a conflagration to rescue a victim.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Be prepared to use CPR if necessary.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is important to have some way to deliver oxygen to your patient if needed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are portable oxygen canisters that can get oxygen quickly into the lungs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont expect a rapid recovery from significant smoke inhalation.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Your patient will be short of breath with the slightest activity and will be very hoarse.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These symptoms may go away with time [Page 76] or may be permanent disabilities.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Planning escape routes and having regular drills will enable your people to get out of dangerous situations quickly.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If everyone knows what to do in advance, you will save precious time.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: STORM PREPAREDNESS There are few people who havent been in the path of a major storm at one point or another.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most of those in the path of an oncoming storm will not have planned for its arrival.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some will even openly flaunt their disregard by seeking exposed areas.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is an instance where a lack of common sense can have dire consequences.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you fail to plan ways to protect yourself and your family, you may find yourself having to treat significant traumatic injuries in the immediate aftermath.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Loss of your shelter may expose your family to hypothermia or heat stroke.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Later, flooding may contaminate your water supplies and expose you to serious infectious disease.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Preparing to weather the storm safely will avoid major medical problems later on.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tornado Preparedness A tornado, or twister, is a violently rotating column of air that is in contact with both the surface of the earth and the thunderstorm (sometimes called a supercell) that spawned it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: From a distance, tornadoes usually appear in the form of a dark funnel with all sorts of flying debris in and around it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_100:20

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Strong winds can carry large objects and fling them around in a manner that is hard to believe.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Indeed, there is a report that, in 1931, an 83-ton train was lifted and thrown 80 feet from the tracks.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although some places may have sirens or other methods of warning of an approaching twister, it is important to have a plan for your family to weather the storm.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Having a plan before a tornado approaches is the most likely way you will survive the event.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you see a twister funnel, take shelter immediately.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They are especially vulnerable to damage from the winds.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you live in Tornado Alley, consider putting together your own underground shelter.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Unlike bunkers and other structures built for long-term protection, a tornado shelter has to provide [Page 77] safety for a short period of time.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As such, it doesnt have to be very large; 8 10 square feet per person would be acceptable.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Despite this, be sure to consider ventilation and the comfort or special needs of those using the shelter.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you dont have a shelter, find a place where family members can gather if a tornado is headed your way.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Basements, bathrooms, closets, or other inside rooms without windows are the best options.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_101
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
