source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Hurricane Preparedness A hurricane is a large tropical storm with winds that have reached a constant speed of 74 miles per hour or more.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In the United States, hurricanes regularly ravage the Gulf of Mexico and the East Coast, causing billions of dollars of damage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Unlike tornados, which can pop up suddenly, hurricanes are first identified when they are hundreds, if not thousands, of miles away.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: We can watch their development and have a good idea of how much time we have to get ready.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Hurricanes are categorized on the basis of severity, using the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Higher-category storms may cause incredible damage and loss of life, such as occurred in Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_102
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: You may also have to make a decision regarding evacuation.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A municipality often will assign a hurricane-resistant public building in [Page 78] your own community as a designated shelter.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you choose to leave town, plan to go as far inland as possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Hurricanes get their strength from the warm water temperatures over the tropical ocean; they lose strength quickly as they travel over land.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although most people pack for seventy-two hours off the grid, that number is relatively arbitrary; be prepared to at least have a weeks supply of food and drinking water, as well as clothes and medical supplies.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You should have an idea of what your homes weak spots are.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Since South Florida was devastated by Hurricane Andrew in 1992, new homes there must have the strength to withstand 125 mph winds.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most homes, however, are made to handle 90 mph.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Hurricane strength is 74 mph.) If the coming storm has sustained winds greater than that, you may not be able to depend on the structural integrity of your home.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you decide to stay, make sure you designate a safe room somewhere in the interior of the house.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It should be in a part of the home most downwind from the direction of the winds.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Make provisions for any animals you will be sheltering and move all outdoor furniture and potted plants either inside the house or up against the outside wall, preferably secured with chains.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:18

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Indoor planning is important, as well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:21

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_103
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_104:0

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_104:1

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_104:2

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_104:4

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_104:5

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In Fukushima, Japan, a powerful earthquake (8.9 on the Richter scale) and tsunami wreaked havoc in 2011, causing major damage, loss of life, and meltdowns in local nuclear reactors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:9

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Make sure each member of your family knows what to do, no matter where they are when an earthquake occurs.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Unless it happens in the dead of night, its unlikely you will all be in the house together.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: To be prepared, youll need, at the very least, the following: Food and water Power sources Alternative shelters Medical supplies Clothing appropriate to the weather Fire extinguishers Means of communication Money (dont count on credit or debit cards being useful if the powers down) An adjustable wrench to turn off gas or water Figure out where youll meet in the event of tremors.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Find out the school systems plan for earthquakes so youll know where to find your kids.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It would be appropriate to, at least, have some food, liquids, and a pair of sturdy, comfortable shoes to keep in your car in an emergency.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_105
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: Asthma Asthma is a chronic condition that affects your ability to breathe.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The following are the main symptoms of asthma: Cough Shortness of breath Wheezing (usually sudden) Chest tightness (sometimes confused with a heart attack) Rapid pulse rate and respiration rate Anxiety Besides these main symptoms, there are others that signal a life-threatening episode.

text: Splinters Being out in the forest or working with wood sometimes leaves a person with a splinter or two to deal with.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can remove a splinter by simply cutting the skin over it until the end can be grasped with small forceps or tweezers.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Youll need a magnifying glass to make this process easier.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you can see the entire length of the splinter, use a scalpel (number 11 or 15 blade) and cut the epidermis.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You want to cut superficially and just enough to expose the tip of the wooden fragment.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Then, take your tweezers and grasp the end of the splinter and pull it out along the angle that it entered the skin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Dont forget to wash the area thoroughly before and after the procedure.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its unlikely that a major infection will come from simply having a splinter, with the exception of those that have been under the skin for more than 23 days.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Redness or swelling in the area will become apparent if an infection is brewing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You might consider antibiotics in this circumstance to avoid having problems later.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Fishhooks Even if youre an accomplished fisherman, you will eventually wind up with a fishhook embedded in you somewhere, probably your hand.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Since the hook probably has worm guts on it, start off by cleaning the area thoroughly with an antiseptic.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Your hook probably has a barbed end.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you cant easily slide it out, the barb is probably the issue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Press down on the skin over where the barb is and then attempt to remove the hook along the curve of the shank.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If this doesnt work, you may have to advance the fishhook further along the [Page 98] skin until the barbed end comes out again.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_130
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: At this point, you can take a wire cutter and separate the barbed end from the shank.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:3

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wash the area again and cover with a bandage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Observe carefully over time for signs of infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: BURN INJURIES If you find yourself off the power grid, you will be cooking out in the open more frequently.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The potential for significant burn injuries will rise exponentially, especially if the survival group includes small children; naturally curious, they may get too close to your campfires.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A working knowledge of burns and their treatment will be a standard skill for every groups medical provider.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The severity of the burn injury depends on the percentage of the total body surface that is burned, and on the degree (depth) of the burn injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although assessing the surface percentage is helpful to burn units in major hospitals, this practice will likely be of limited helpfulness in austere settings.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Before we discuss the different degrees of burn you might encounter, lets talk about prevention.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most burns youll see will be due to too much exposure to the sun.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Take the following steps to avoid sunburn: Stay out of the sun whenever possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid work during peak sun hours (say, 11 a.m.4 p.m.).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wear long pants and sleeves, hats, and sunglasses.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Spend rest periods in the shade.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you cannot avoid extended exposure to sunlight, be certain to apply a sunblock.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Do this before going outside and frequently throughout the day.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Even water resistant and waterproof sunscreens should be reapplied generously every 12 hours.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: By the way, a sunblock and a sunscreen are not the same thing.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sunblock contains tiny particles that block and reflect ultraviolet (UV) light; sunscreen contains substances that absorb UV light, thus preventing it from penetrating the skin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many commercial products contain both.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The SPF (sun protection factor) rating system was developed in 1962 to measure the capacity of a product to block UV radiation.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An SPF of at least 15 is recommended.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It takes about 20 minutes without sunscreen for your skin to turn red.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_131
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A product that is SPF 15 should delay burning by a factor of 15, or about 5 hours

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: to measure the capacity of a product to block UV radiation.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An SPF of at least 15 is recommended.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It takes about 20 minutes without sunscreen for your skin to turn red.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A product that is SPF 15 should delay burning by a factor of 15, or about 5 hours or so.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Higher SPF ratings give more protection, and are beneficial to those with fair skin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Besides the sun, injuries will most likely be related to cooking and managing campfires.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Using hand protection will prevent many of these burns, as will careful supervision of children near any cooking area.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Burns are traditionally assessed by degree of damage, as described below.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: First-Degree Burns These burns will be very common, such as simple sunburn.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The injury will appear red, warm and dry, and will be painful to the touch.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These burns frequently affect large areas of the torso; immersion in a cool bath or running cool water over the injury is helpful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: [Page 99] Placing a cool moist cloth on the area will give some relief, as will common anti-inflammatory medicines such as ibuprofen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Aloe vera or zinc-oxide cream is also an effective treatment.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Usually, the discomfort improves after 24 hours or so, as only the superficial skin layer, the epidermis, is affected.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid tight clothing and try to wear light fabrics, such as cotton.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Second-Degree Burns These burns are deeper, going partially through the skin, and will be seen to be moist and have blisters with reddened bases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The area will have a tendency to weep clear or whitish fluid.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The area will become somewhat swollen, so remove rings and bracelets.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Treat second-degree burns as follows: Run cool water over the injury for 1015 minutes (avoid ice).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Give oral pain relief, such as ibuprofen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Apply anesthetic ointments or gels.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use silver sulfadiazine (Silvadene) creams to help prevent infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Lance only large blisters.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Avoid peeling off burned skin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:24
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Apply nonstick skin dressings.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:25
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Third-Degree Burns Third-degree burns involve the full thickness of skin and possibly deeper structures, such as subcutaneous fat and muscle.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:26
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The burned skin may appear charred or white.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:27
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The burn may appear indented if significant tissue has been lost.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:28
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Third-degree burns will cause dehydration, so giving fluids is essential to keep the patient stable.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132:29
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_132
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_137
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once they bite you, however, they tend to hold on; pit vipers prefer to bite and let go quickly.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_139:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_139
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_139
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The hairs and fibers on some caterpillars carry toxins that can also deliver a painful sting that, unless the victim has a severe allergic reaction, is not life threatening.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_139
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: and does not necessarily include loss of consciousness.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Indeed, most concussions are not associated with loss of consciousness.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If brief loss of consciousness does occur, the patient will usually awaken somewhat foggy, and may be unclear as to how the injury occurred or the events shortly before or after.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Effects are usually temporary but can include headaches (the most common symptom), ringing in the ears, dizziness, and problems with concentration, memory, balance, and coordination.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They may appear sluggish or tired.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is important to be certain that the patient, once awake, has regained normal motor function.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In other words, make sure they can move all their extremities with normal range and strength.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Even so, rest is prescribed for a day or two, so that they may be closely watched.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Acetaminophen should be given for headache instead of aspirin or ibuprofen, because of the risk of bleeding.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its OK to let your patient get some sleep.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Once asleep, it might be appropriate to awaken them about every 2 hours to make sure that they can be aroused and have developed none of the danger signals mentioned.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In most cases, a concussion causes no permanent damage if further trauma is avoided.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Multiple episodes of head trauma over time, howeveras in the case of boxers or some other athletescan lead to long-term brain damage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This can manifest as follows: Memory deficits Personality changes Sleep disturbances Seizures Psychological problems such as depression Disorders of taste and smell Sensitivity to light and noise If the period of unconsciousness is more than 10 minutes in length, you must suspect the possibility of significant injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Vital signs, such as pulse, respiration rate, [Page 108] and blood pressure, should be monitored closely.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patients head should be immobilized, in case there is damage to the spine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Verify that the airway is clear, and remove any possible obstructions.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without advanced care, this person will be in a life-threatening situation, with few options, if consciousness is not regained.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: SPRAINS AND STRAINS Bones, joints, muscles, and tendons give the body support and locomotion, and there is no substitute for having all your parts in good working order.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The amount of work these structures will be called upon to do after a disaster will be greatly increased.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_144
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, the medic will expect to see more injuries; it is important to know how to identify and treat these problems.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: your parts in good working order.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The amount of work these structures will be called upon to do after a disaster will be greatly increased.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, the medic will expect to see more injuries; it is important to know how to identify and treat these problems.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Many people have heard of ligaments, tendons, sprains, and strains but have little idea of what they really are.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:4:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, lets define some anatomical terms: Jointthe physical point of connection between two bones, usually enabling a certain range of motion, for example, the knee or elbow joint Ligamentthe fibrous tissue that connects one bone to another, oftentimes across a joint Tendontissue that extends from muscle to connect to bone Sprainan injury where a ligament is excessively stretched by forcing a joint beyond its normal range of motion Strainwhen the muscle or its connection to the bone (tendon) is partially torn as a result of an injury Rupturea complete tear through a ligament or muscle Sprains Our joints are truly marvels of engineering.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They help provide mobility and locomotion and sometimes bear an incredible amount of stress without mishap.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They are moving parts, however, and moving parts wear down.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In a disaster, our level of physical exertion may increase; the risk of injury to the joints increases as well.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can expect the most common sprains in your group to involve the ankle, wrist, knee, or finger.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most likely signs and symptoms are bruising, swelling, and pain.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Treatment for most sprains is relatively straightforward and follows the easy- to-remember RICES protocol: Rest.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is important to avoid further injury by not testing the injured joint.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Stop whatever actions led to the injury, and you will have the best chance to recover fully.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Cold therapy decreases both swelling and pain.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The earlier it is applied, the more likely it will speed up the healing process.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If youre in the wilderness, have some instant cold packs in your backpack, as ice may be unavailable.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Cold therapy should be performed several times a day for 2030 minutes or so each time for the first 2448 hours.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is followed each time by applying compression.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A compression bandage is useful to decrease swelling and should be applied after each cold therapy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This will also help provide support to the joint.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_145
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: After applying some padding to the area, securely wrap an elastic bandage, starting below the joint

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is followed each time by applying compression.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A compression bandage is useful to decrease swelling and should be applied after each cold therapy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This will also help provide support to the joint.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: After applying some padding to the area, securely wrap an elastic bandage, starting below the joint and working [Page 109] your way up beyond it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Any tingling, increased pain, or numbness tells you that the wrap is too tight and should be loosened.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: An excessively tight wrap may affect the circulation and cause fingertips to turn white or even blue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Elevate the sprain above the level of the heart.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This will help decrease swelling at the site of the injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: By elevating the leg, you allow inflammatory fluid to process itself back into your circulation and aid the healing process, or at least not impede it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This also works for swollen ankles due to chronic medical problems, like high blood pressure; even pregnant women achieve relief from swollen ankles in this fashion.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Immobilizing the injury will prevent further damage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This may be accomplished by the compression bandage alone or may require a splint or a cast.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the patient is unable to place much weight on the joint, this strategy will be especially useful.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pillow splint Splints may be commercially produced, such as the very useful SAM (structural aluminum malleable) splint, or may be improvised with sticks and cloth or pillows and duct tape.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Make sure the injured joint is immobile after placement of the splint.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: How can you tell the difference between a sprain and a fracture?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Sometimes its quite easy, as when a straight bone is suddenly zig-zag in shape.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Often its quite difficult to determine without modern diagnostic tests.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You can, however, look for one or more of these signs that an injury may relate to a fracture rather than a sprain: A fracture will generally have more pronounced swelling and bruising.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture is generally so painful that no traction or pressure may be placed on the injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture may have a deep cut in the area of the injury (called an open fracture, which is particularly dangerous because of the risk of infection).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture may show motion in an area beyond the joint (if your finger suddenly has five knuckles, you probably broke it).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_146
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture may present a grating sensation when the point of the break

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: injury (called an open fracture, which is particularly dangerous because of the risk of infection).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:1
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture may show motion in an area beyond the joint (if your finger suddenly has five knuckles, you probably broke it).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A fracture may present a grating sensation when the point of the break is pressed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For sprains, ibuprofen serves as both an anti-inflammatory and pain reliever.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most sprains heal well over time using the RICES protocol, pain relievers, and a lot of rest.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Others, however, such as severe knee sprains with torn or ruptured ligaments, may heal completely only with the aid of surgical intervention.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its important to get joint issues dealt with while we still have modern medicine to help us.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you need surgery to fix a bad knee, do it now.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In uncertain times, you (and your joints) want to be in the best shape possible to face the challenges ahead.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Strains By far, the most frequently seen strain will be to the back muscles.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Strains, especially back strains, involve injury to the muscle and their tendons (which connects them to the bone).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the lower part of the back holds the majority of the bodys weight, you can expect the most trouble here.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: [Page 110] Some of these injuries are preventable with some simple precautions: Every morning you should perform some stretching, to increase blood flow to cold, stiff muscles and joints.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When you lift a heavy object, such as a backpack, keep your back straight and let your legs perform the work.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The object should be close to your body as you lift it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Dont reach for it.) For packs, keep the weight on the hips rather than the shoulders.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you are on rocky or unstable terrain, consider using a walking stick for balance.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Remember, any weight-lifting action that you perform while being off-balance is likely to result in a strained muscle.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Moist heat therapy seems to be effective for relief in back strains.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Ibuprofen is an excellent anti- inflammatory and pain reliever for these types of injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_147:20

text: DISLOCATIONS A dislocation is an injury in which a bone is pulled out of its joint by some type of trauma.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In open fractures, the skin is pierced by the broken bone or there is some other penetrating trauma.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Needless to say, there is usually more blood loss and infection associated with an open wound.
