chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_149
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For most fractures, you will want to consider the placement of a cast to enforce immobilization.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Casting material using plaster of Paris or fiberglass is easy to obtain and lasts a long time.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its a useful addition to any medical storage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When placing a cast, you will first start with a liner of cotton known as a stockinette.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Then, you will need rolls of padding to form a barrier between the skin and the cast.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Rolls of plaster of Paris or fiberglass are then immersed in water for 20 seconds or so.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Wring out the excess water.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: (Keep the end of the roll between your fingers or it will stick and be difficult to find.) Then, begin to slowly roll the casting material around the area of the fracture, smoothing it out [Page 113] as you go along.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Advance one-half of the thickness of the roll as you go from beyond the fracture towards the torso.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You will want perhaps three layers of casting material on the area, more in places where there is a bony prominence, such as the wrist.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Each fracture is casted somewhat differently, and stockinettes, padding, and casting rolls are available in different widths and lengths appropriate to the particular fracture.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_151
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Most fractures require 6 8 weeks to form a callous, newly formed tissue that will reunite the broken ends of the bone.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:6

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the fracture is not realigned well, the function of the affected extremity can be permanently compromised.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Rib Fractures and Pneumothorax Rib fractures are commonly treated by firmly taping the affected area, as it is the motion of breathing that causes the pain associated with the injury.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although reduction is usually not necessary, taping the area may help provide pain relief.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Rib fractures become more serious if the fracture punctures a lung.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This causes a pneumothorax (collapsed lung), a condition in which air from the puncture enters the chest cavity, compressing the lung and collapsing the organ.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although a person with a rib fracture will complain of pain with breathing, a person with a pneumothorax will have signs of bluish skin coloration (cyanosis), distended neck veins, and signs of shock.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you use a stethoscope, you will hear the sounds snap, crackle, and pop, familiarly associated with Rice KrispiesTM cereal when you listen to the lungs, or perhaps no breath sounds at all from the affected area.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If the pneumothorax has become life threatening, known as a tension pneumothorax, you may have to decompress the lung.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This should only be attempted if its clear the patient will die without this action being taken.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Clean the area of the chest above the third rib, midway between the top of the shoulder and the nipple.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Using a sharp object no wider than a pencil, poke a hole above the rib (the blood vessels travel below the rib) deep enough to hear air pass through.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_152
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A large-gauge (14 or larger) decompression needle is commercially available.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:5

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: Inflammatory or bloody fluid is likely to accumulate in many lung wounds.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It will not, however, be as efficient as the electric suction systems available at your local hospital.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its important to realize that chest wounds will be difficult to recover from without advanced care.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: AMPUTATION In rare circumstances, damage to a limb may be so extensive that it cannot be saved.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Amputation is the surgical removal of all or part of an extremity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This procedure is performed on arms, legs, hands, feet, fingers, or toes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The closer to the torso that the amputation was performed, the higher the death rate will be.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Amputation, even in a survival situation, is a last resort.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In many cases, your patient will not survive it.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: At least 25 percent of American Civil War soldiers undergoing the procedure by trained personnel lost their lives because of bleeding or infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:18:0
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Having said that, there are various reasons why amputation might be necessary: Damaged blood vessels that fail to provide oxygen to tissue Extensive injury from trauma or burns Cancerous tumors Severe frostbite Gangrene Look for the following to identify where to cut and how much to remove: Where an extremity loses a pulse Areas when a limb loses normal temperature Areas of reddened skin (infection) or blackened skin (gangrene) The place where the extremity is no longer sensitive to touch Areas where the bone has been crushed beyond repair The following are basic measures to increase the chances of a successful amputation: Sedate the patient as much as possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_153
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Clean the damaged area with Betadine or other antiseptics before

text: The place where the extremity is no longer sensitive to touch Areas where the bone has been crushed beyond repair The following are basic measures to increase the chances of a successful amputation: Sedate the patient as much as possible.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:1

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:2
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Use sterile gloves in a sterile field.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Remove debris and bits of shattered bone.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Tie off bleeding blood vessels.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Preserve an adequate amount of living tissue to cover the exposed end of the bone.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Shorten and smooth the bone enough to decrease irritation to the covering soft tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Stitch remaining muscle to the bone lining (periosteum), which is difficult without special equipment.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Before closing completely, place a drain (discussed earlier in this book) to enable blood and inflammatory fluid to leave the surgical site.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Adequately close the wound with sutures or staples.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Change dressings regularly.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Observe for infection and, if present, start a course of antibiotics.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Amputation is a procedure we hope you will never have to consider.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In severe injuries, however, it may be an avenue of last resort.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: CHRONIC MEDICAL PROBLEMS As a caregiver in a long-term survival scenario, you cannot expect that everyone under your care will start off in perfect health.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It is likely that one or more members of your family or group will have a long-standing medical issue that cannot be ignored.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Thyroid malfunction, [Page 115] diabetes, and heart disease are just some of these issues.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: They require medications that will not be manufactured in times of trouble.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You must, therefore, think outside the box to formulate a medical strategy for these patients that does not include modern technology.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It goes without saying that medical conditions that are poorly controlled now could be completely out of control in a survival setting.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most important way to preserve your familys health will be to have any chronic conditions appropriately treated and monitored before a catastrophe.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this section we discuss some chronic problems with which the medic may have to deal.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you ever find yourself on your own, having a plan in place will increase your effectiveness as caregiver and improve the health of the community.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_154
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: THYROID DISEASE The thyroid gland is positioned just in front of and below the Adams apple (laryngeal prominence) and produces hormones that help regulate your metabolism.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The organ produces substances that regulate growth, energy, and the bodys use of other hormones and vitamins.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Thyroid conditions usually involve the production of either too little or too much of these hormones.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: These malfunctions are more commonly seen in women.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A thyroid problem that might be common in an austere setting is the development of a goiter, a lump on the thyroid.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This is the result of a deficiency of iodine in the body and is one of the reasons why iodine is added to common table salt, making it iodized.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Potassium iodide tablets may be a treatment option if no other source of iodine is available.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_155
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: Hyperthyroidism Hyperthyroidism is the excessive production of thyroid hormone.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The following are some common signs and symptoms of this condition in adults: Insomnia Hand tremors Nervousness Feeling excessively hot in normal or cold temperatures Eyes appearing to be bulging out or staring Frequent bowel movements Losing weight despite normal or increased appetite Excessive sweating Weight loss Menstrual irregularities Growth and puberty issues (children) Muscle weakness, chest pain, and shortness of breath (elderly) Poorly controlled hyperthyroidism can lead to a condition known as thyroid storm, in which large levels of hormone have major effects on the heart and brain.

text: Hypothyroidism More commonly seen than hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism is the failure to produce enough thyroid hormone.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_156
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_156
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The following are the most commonly seen signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism in adults: Fatigue Intolerance to cold Constipation Poor appetite Weight gain Dry skin Hair loss Hoarseness Depression Menstrual irregularity Poor growth (in children) Long-standing untreated hypothyroidism may result in thickened skin, hair loss (alopecia), vocal changes, and swelling.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Such replacements come in a variety of dosages, and it is important to determine the appropriate one for your patient while modern medical care is still available.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Besides standard thyroid medications, such as SynthroidTM and LevothroidTM, there are a number of other remedies that may improve hypothyroidism.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: DIABETES Diabetes is a common, yet devastating, disease characterized by high sugar (glucose) levels in the blood.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Uncontrolled diabetes is known to cause damage to various organs, such as the kidneys, eyes, and heart.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The incidence of the disease has been increasing over time in developed countries, perhaps because of issues relating to obesity.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diabetes is especially problematic for the survival medic in that the medications used to treat the worst cases are unlikely to be produced in a grid-down scenario.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diabetic medications, such as insulin, lose potency over time.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, an alternative strategy to keep diabetics from losing complete control of their blood sugar will have to be formulated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are two types of diabetes.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Type 1 results from the failure of the pancreas to produce insulin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Insulin is a hormone that controls the level of sugar in your system.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The destruction of the cells in the pancreas that produce insulin is thought to be caused by an autoimmune response.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This means that the bodys own immune system attacks parts of itself.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Type 1 diabetes is often first diagnosed in childhood.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Type 2 diabetes is more commonly the result of the resistance of the cells in your body to the insulin produced by the pancreas.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Obesity is thought to be a major factor.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In type 2 diabetes, certain cells do not respond appropriately to insulin.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Glucose fails to enter these cells and, therefore, it accumulates in the blood.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: High blood sugar is known as hyperglycemia.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Diabetes (mild or severe) may also develop in some pregnancies, even in nondiabetic women.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Some believe that those who get diabetes during their pregnancies may be prone to diabetic issues later in life.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157:23
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are three classic symptoms of diabetes: Extreme thirst Excessive hunger Frequent urination Uncontrolled diabetes causes eye and kidney problems, leading to blindness and renal failure.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_157
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are two main types of gallstones: Cholesterol stonesThe grand majority, these are not related to the actual cholesterol levels in the bloodstream.

text: Risk factors for gallstones include obesity, female gender (especially if they have had children), and age over forty.

text: Symptoms of biliary colic include the following: Cramping right upper abdomen pain (spreading to the back) Fever Jaundice (yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes) Discolored bowel movements (gray or grayish-white) Nausea and vomiting The classical finding on physical examination is Murphys sign.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: OTHER IMPORTANT MEDICAL ISSUES CPR IN AUSTERE SETTINGS Most medical books start off with a chapter on cardio-pulmonary resuscitation, so you might wonder why this subject has not been given coverage so far in this volume.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The answer is based on hard realities that we must confront in a survival scenario.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although CPR is an important skill that everyone should know, there are fewer situations in a collapse scenario where it will return a victim to normal function.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are only a small number of circumstances where a patient goes from being a patient in need of resuscitation to a person who is back to normal.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: CPR is best used as a stabilization strategy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You want to get the heart pumping and breathing supported so that you can get your patient as quickly as possible to a facility where there are ventilators, defibrillators, and other high technology.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: But what about a situation where this technology is no longer available?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There wont be cardiac bypasses for your patient who has had a heart attack.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There wont be surgical suites for your patient with a shotgun blast to the abdomen or chest.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The sobering truth is that many of these injuries will be mortal wounds.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This means that death is [Page 129] the inevitable end result, no matter what you try to do.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The poor prognosis for these people in hard times is tragic; it makes you truly appreciate the benefits of modern medicine.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There are still instances, however, where CPR may actually restore a gravely ill person to normal function.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Environmental conditions, such as hypothermia, heat stroke, or smoke inhalation, will often respond to resuscitative efforts with complete recovery.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_172
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Severe anaphylactic reactions may require CPR until the patient responds to epinephrine (EpiPen) and resolves the attack.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If you see a conscious adult in sudden respiratory distress, ask quickly, Are you choking on something?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_173
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: BIRTH CONTROL, PREGNANCY, AND DELIVERY Its a rare individual who doesnt have a wife, girlfriend, mother, daughter or granddaughter that isnt of childbearing age (1350 years old).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:8
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In a long-term disaster, society will be unstable and organized medical care will be spotty at best, nonexistent at worst.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: One of the least welcome events might be one that, for many families, is ordinarily considered a blessing: a pregnancy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A pregnancy and the possible complications that accompany it will be a burden in a disaster.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A pregnant woman will be at less than 100 percent efficiency at the exact wrong time, and complications could occur.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The death rate among pregnant women (also known as the maternal mortality rate) at the time of the American Revolution was about 24 percent per pregnancy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Given that the average woman in the year 1800 could expect 610 pregnancies over the course of her reproductive life, the cumulative maternal mortality rate easily approached 25 percent.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: That means that one out of four women died from complications of being pregnant, either early, during the childbirth, or even soon after a successful delivery.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: If a major disaster occurs, women might face unacceptable levels of risk.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: There wont be either medicine or medical supplies in which to treat pregnancy and childbirth complications.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Deaths may happen simply because there are no IV fluids or medications to stop bleeding or treat infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When a pregnancy goes wrong, it takes away a valuable contributor from the family (sometimes permanently) and places an additional strain on resources and manpower.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pregnancy Complications The reasons that women could cease to become productive group members (or even die) during pregnancy or childbirth include the following: Hyperemesis gravidarum.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Simply put, this is excessive vomiting in early pregnancy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Everyones nauseous when theyre pregnant, but a few will have such extreme vomiting as to become severely dehydrated.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188:22
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_188
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without IV fluid replacement,

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:3
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without IV fluid replacement, some of these patients might not survive.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:4

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Approximately 10 percent of all pregnancies end in miscarriage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: When a woman miscarries, she might not pass all of the dead tissue relating to the pregnancy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This tissue may become infected or cause excessive bleeding.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:7

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The treatment in this case would be dilatation and curettage (D&C), a procedure in which [Page 141] scrapers called curettes are used to remove the retained tissue.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:8

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without the right equipment and experience, some women might succumb.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pregnancy-induced hypertension.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Blood pressure may rise to dangerous levels and cause alarming amounts of swelling, sometimes throughout the body.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This mostly is seen in the last 3 months of a first pregnancy.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without modern facilities, bed rest (lying on the left side is best) may be just about all that you can do.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The delivery itself, although usually straightforward, can be fraught with complications.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Excessive bleeding could occur before, during or after delivery due to vaginal tears or premature separation of the placenta from the uterus.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The placenta ordinarily is expelled spontaneously within minutes after the delivery; however, there are occasions where it is stuck and must be manually removed.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In these cases, portions of the placenta may remain lodged in the uterine walls, leading to bleeding and/or infection.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:18
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Failure of the uterine walls to contract after delivery may also cause hemorrhage.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:19
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Pregnancy Care Basics You may find yourself responsible for the care of a pregnant woman.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:20
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It will be important to know how to support that pregnancy and, eventually, deliver that baby.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189:21
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Without access to prenatal megavitamins, babies will be smaller at birth.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_189
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Although your pregnant patient will not be as productive for the survival group as she would ordinarily be, she will probably still be able to contribute to help make your efforts a success.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The medic will need to know pregnancy care and how to deliver the fetus.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Today, we have simple tests that can identify pregnancy almost before a woman misses her period, but what if these tests are no longer available?

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:6
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: You will have to rely on the following tried and true signs and symptoms to identify the condition: Absent menstruation Tender breasts Nausea and vomiting Darkening of the nipples, areola, or both Fatigue Frequent urination Backache These symptoms, in combination, indicate pregnancy.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The timing of each will be variable: some will be noticed earlier than others.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: It should be noted that this investigation will be necessary only in those women experiencing their first pregnancy.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

text: For more about the monitoring and care of a pregnancy, consider getting a copy [Page 142] of our book The Survival Medicine Handbook.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:13
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The patients abdomen may look different, or the top of the uterus (fundus) may appear lower.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As the neck of the uterus (cervix) relaxes, the patient may notice a mucus-like discharge, sometimes with a bloody component.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190:17

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_190

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Frequent vaginal exams are invasive, however, and not necessary in most cases.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191:4
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Contractions will start becoming more frequent.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191:5
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_191
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: A gush of watery fluid from the vagina will often signify the water breaking (rupture of the amniotic sac) and is also a sign of impending labor and delivery.

text: PAIN MEDICATIONS It stands to reason that minor issues with discomfort now will be multiplied by the increased workload demands of a power-down situation.

source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Therefore, any person who hasnt considered providing for pain issues in times of trouble is not medically prepared.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:7
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Its a good idea to have a working knowledge of the actions and uses of various pain medications.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: As pain is variable, there are many different types of drugs available that have different mechanisms of action for pain relief (analgesia), as described below.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:9
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAIDS): These drugs act to decrease inflammation and fever as well as pain.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:10
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most popular NSAIDs are ibuprofen and aspirin; naproxen is another NSAID that is available without a prescription.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:11
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: For quick relief from pain, the shorter-acting ibuprofen or aspirin is superior to naproxen.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:12
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Naproxen may not have an effect until a couple of doses, but works well for long-term relief.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Acetaminophen: This drug relieves pain by changing the bodys sensitivity to things that cause pain (its pain threshold), and also lowers fever.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:14
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: This drug is often as effective as NSAIDs for pain and has fewer side effects (unless you have liver disease).

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:15
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Acetaminophen has no anti- inflammatory action, however; therefore, it may be less effective than NSAIDs [Page 147] for some conditions.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:16
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: Steroids: Corticosteroids exert their effect upon pain by a very strong anti- inflammatory action.

id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197:17
chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: The most common steroids used for inflammation are prednisone and cortisone.

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_197

text: How to Use Antibiotics There are many antibiotics, but which that are accessible to the average person would be good additions to your medical storage?

chunk_id: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015_chunk_203
source: The Ultimate Survival Medicine Guide - Emergency Preparedness for Any Disaster 2015
text: In this section, we discuss antibiotics (all available in veterinary form without a prescription) that you will want in your medical arsenal: Amoxicillin 250 mg or 500 mg (Fish Mox, Fish Mox Forte) Ciprofloxacin 250 mg or 500 mg (Fish Flox, Fish Flox Forte) Cephalexin 250 mg or 500 mg (Fish Flex, Fish Flex Forte) Metronidazole 250 mg (Fish Zole) Doxycycline 100 mg (Bird Biotic) Ampicillin 250 mg or 500 mg (Fish Cillin, Fish Cillin Forte) Sulfamethoxazole 400 mg/Trimethoprim 80 mg (Bird Sulfa) Clindamycin 150 mg (Fish Cin) Azithromycin 250 mg (Aquatic Azithromycin) There are various others that you can choose, but these selections will give you the opportunity to treat many illnesses and have enough variety so that even those with penicillin allergies will have options.
